item.title: Finance Pulse - Jul 24, 2026
item.description:
Now I have comprehensive data across all required coverage areas. Let me build today's full briefing.
---
## Finance Pulse | Friday, July 24, 2026
**Bottom line: June CPI's sharp drop to three point five percent changes the rate-path calculus heading into Tuesday's FOMC, giving bank CFOs a momentary reprieve on deposit repricing assumptions, but Huntington's Cadence conversion close-out this week is the real operating-model story: the last major integration milestone in the cohort is done, and the synergy clock has started -- making post-merger finance-function integration the week's sharpest transformation signal.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. The annual inflation rate in the US fell to three point five percent in June 2026, the first decline in five months, compared to four point two percent in May and below forecasts of three point eight percent. That disinflation is energy-driven and incomplete -- core still matters -- but it materially shifts the July twenty-nine FOMC calculus.
2. Huntington completed its Cadence systems conversion and is now shifting focus to growth, with management targeting three hundred sixty-five million dollars in Cadence cost synergies by Q4, and Brant Standridge noted the bank completed the Cadence systems conversion two hundred thirty-five days after announcement. That speed-to-close benchmark is now the standard every bank CFO in an active integration will be measured against.
3. On June tenth, the Financial Stability Board published its first operational framework for governing agentic AI in financial services, covering twelve sound practices across board accountability, lifecycle management, and AI-monitoring-AI architectures, with comments closing July twenty-second. The comment window just closed, and a final report to G20 finance ministers is due in October -- meaning governance requirements for agentic AI in banks are now crystallizing into hard policy.
4. The blanket ten percent tariff under Section one-twenty-two expires today, July twenty-four, twenty-twenty-six, and the administration has announced plans to implement tariffs under Section three-oh-one. For bank CFOs, this is a planning inflection point: the tariff structure your macro scenario assumed as of yesterday is legally different today.
5. More than half of CFOs -- fifty-four percent, according to Deloitte's 2026 CFO Signals Survey -- have named integrating AI agents into their finance function as their single biggest digital transformation priority this year.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The tariff cliff as a live CFO planning event** Today is the expiration date of the Section one-twenty-two blanket ten percent tariff. After the Supreme Court's February ruling that emergency-power tariffs were illegal, the administration implemented the ten percent blanket tariff under Section one-twenty-two -- which expires today -- and has announced plans to shift to Section three-oh-one authority. For a bank CFO or treasurer, this is not a macro backdrop item. It is an active variable in credit-loss provisioning models (client supply chains), in FX and liquidity stress scenarios, and in the forward assumptions underpinning the next planning cycle. The transition from one-twenty-two to three-oh-one also changes the legal architecture of future tariffs, making their durability harder to model.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): Disinflation arrives, but the Fed is not done** The annual inflation rate fell to three point five percent in June, the first decline in five months, as the ceasefire between the US and Iran alleviated inflationary pressures from the energy component. However, Fed Governor Lisa Cook noted that even after softer CPI and PPI prints this week, the price index the Fed targets still rose three point seven percent in the twelve months through June -- one point seven percentage points above the two percent target. For bank CFOs, the practical implication is that markets are pricing in a high probability of rates remaining unchanged at the July FOMC meeting, but the rate path beyond July is still live. Futures markets are pricing a path that rises to about three point eight percent by October twenty twenty-six and approaches four percent around year-end. That forward curve is the central planning assumption for NII models and deposit cost projections right now.
**Theme 3 (New): The Huntington integration close-out as a finance transformation case study** Huntington's total revenue grew forty-six percent year-over-year to two point eight six billion dollars in Q2, with net interest income rising forty percent year-over-year to two point zero five billion dollars. But the finance function story is in the machinery behind that scale: with the Veritex, Janney and TM Capital, and Cadence integrations behind them, management now has strong line of sight to remaining cost synergies and is actively driving revenue synergies, expecting the full earnings power of these partnerships to be clearly evident by Q4. The systems conversion completion included one hundred fifty-two million dollars of pre-tax acquisition-related notable items -- a visible cost of integration that every bank CFO considering M&A should underwrite into their business case.
---
### Banking Finance-Function
**NIM and Funding Costs: Post-Rate-Peak Repricing**
The Huntington print offers the clearest cross-cohort read on integration-driven NIM pressure. Huntington's net interest margin increased ten basis points year-over-year but declined three basis points sequentially. The sequential decline reflected higher funding costs and the full-quarter impact of the Cadence balance sheet. This is a direct consequence of absorbing an acquired deposit book: the repricing friction is real, and it is temporary -- but it requires the finance function to model a trough and a recovery arc simultaneously.
Elsewhere in the Q2 reporting tail, smaller banks are demonstrating that NIM expansion without rate cuts is achievable. Metropolitan Bank Holding reported a net interest margin of four point zero eight percent for the quarter, with management noting that adjusting conservatively for excess cash held at the Federal Reserve, the normalized NIM would have been above four point one five percent. Critically, their expanding NIM forecast is not reliant on rate cut assumptions, using no movement in the Fed funds target rate as the baseline. That is precisely the modeling discipline bank CFOs need to demonstrate to boards right now.
**Wholesale Funding Reduction as Strategic Priority**
Bankwell Financial reduced its wholesale funding by forty-three point seven million dollars in Q2, lowering the wholesale ratio to sixteen point three percent from twenty-one point two percent at year-end, and has reduced brokered deposits by fifty point six percent from their peak of over one billion dollars at year-end 2022. The structural shift away from brokered and wholesale funding toward core deposits is a multi-quarter CFO agenda item -- it improves funding cost, reduces interest rate sensitivity, and strengthens FDIC stress metrics all at once.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Proposal: Now in the Post-Comment Finalization Window**
On March nineteenth, federal banking agencies issued three proposals to revise the US bank capital framework, marking the most significant reset to the regime in more than a decade. The changes could materially affect bank capital requirements, profitability, product and service offerings, and long-term growth strategies. Overall, bank capital requirements are expected to decrease across the industry due to lower minimum risk weights, less conservative methodologies, lower buffers and surcharges, and a narrower application of the market risk framework.
The operationally important angle for finance teams: although the proposals may relieve certain capital pressures, the 2026 capital rules also add complexity and will require careful implementation. That complexity is where the finance transformation demand lives -- new data taxonomies, new RWA calculation flows, and new reporting pipelines.
The Federal Reserve has reopened comment on its March 2026 proposal partly to analyze AI implications, and the BIS Innovation Hub is running pilot projects that test supervisory large language models for call-report validation. That second signal matters: regulators are themselves experimenting with AI-driven oversight, which changes the error-detection bar for banks' own regulatory submissions.
**FSB Agentic AI Governance: Comment Period Just Closed**
The FSB June 2026 consultation -- the first global framework to treat agentic AI as operationally distinct -- identifies six oversight models for agentic systems and recommends human-in-command for high-autonomy workflows, AI-in-the-loop monitoring as agent populations grow, and human approval or dual authorization for agents executing financial transactions above threshold values. Comments closed July twenty-second, with a final report to G20 finance ministers expected in October 2026. Banks that built agentic AI pilots in treasury or regulatory reporting without governance scaffolding now have a concrete global benchmark against which to remediate.
---
### AI in Finance
**The Agentic AI Governance Gap is Now Closing -- Fast**
The FSB framework comment period just closed. For bank CFOs who have been deploying agentic AI in FP&A or close automation, the October G20 report is a hard governance deadline to plan against. The framework's "dual authorization for agents executing financial transactions above threshold values" language is directly relevant to any treasury or payment-adjacent AI deployment.
Deloitte's 2026 CFO Signals Survey found that fifty-four percent of CFOs have named integrating AI agents into their finance function as their single biggest digital transformation priority this year. But the buying pattern is maturing past aspiration: finance teams getting the most out of agentic AI in 2026 started with a single, well-defined, high-pain workflow -- usually invoice processing or financial reconciliation -- established the governance layer properly, demonstrated measurable results, and then expanded from there.
**ROI Reality Check vs. Vendor Claims**
IDC reports that organizations achieve an average two point three times return on agentic AI investments within thirteen months, with ROI expected to grow as adoption of AI scales. That figure is an aggregate across industries and should be treated as directional rather than bankable for a CFO business case. The more important discipline for bank finance functions is the requirement to re-architect data governance and process flows before agentic AI can deliver at scale -- an investment that is often invisible in vendor ROI claims but material in implementation reality.
Gartner predicts that agentic AI will make fifteen percent of everyday work decisions and augment thirty-three percent of enterprise software applications by 2028 -- but also predicts that over forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027. For finance transformation consultants, that cancellation forecast is the most useful framing in a client conversation: governance failure and poor workflow scoping, not technology inadequacy, drive project mortality.
**Where CFO Budgets Are Actually Flowing**
CFOs are dedicating roughly twenty-five percent of their budgets to AI agents and anticipating approximately twenty percent lifts in revenue or cost savings. The workflow sequencing evidence suggests reconciliation and close automation are the first dollar spent, regulatory reporting automation is the second, and FP&A scenario modeling is the third -- in that order of maturity and deployability.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**Post-Integration Synergy Execution as a Finance Function Test**
Huntington's transition from integration to synergy capture is the live template. Management expressed confidence in achieving its 2027 ROTCE target of eighteen to nineteen percent, with plans for continued share repurchase and organic growth. The finance function must now own the synergy tracking infrastructure -- cost saves against the three hundred sixty-five million dollar target, revenue synergy attribution, and operating leverage measurement. That is a data and reporting architecture problem, not just a planning one.
**The "No Rate Cut" NII Planning Baseline is Consolidating**
Across the Q2 earnings cohort, management teams are converging on a no-rate-cut base case for second-half NII guidance. Western Alliance's 2026 outlook assumed no rate cuts in 2026, with NII guidance tracking towards the upper end of its eleven to fourteen percent growth range. That consensus baseline gives finance teams a clear anchor: plan for flat rates, model a hike scenario as the upside stress case, and size deposit cost assumptions accordingly.
**Tariff Transition as a Planning-Cycle Disruptor**
Today's Section one-twenty-two expiration and the shift to Section three-oh-one creates a genuine model-update obligation for CFOs with material credit exposure to import-dependent borrowers. Scenario libraries need a refreshed tariff chapter by end of next week if they are going to be useful for the Q3 planning cycle.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The banking industry consensus is treating the FSB's new agentic AI governance framework as a compliance burden. The contrarian read is the opposite: it is a procurement accelerant. Banks that can demonstrate FSB-aligned governance -- board accountability, lifecycle management, dual authorization controls -- will have a differentiated procurement story when buying agentic AI from EPM and ERP vendors. Every vendor selling into the CFO office will be asked to show how their product maps to the FSB's twelve sound practices. The banks that write that requirements document first will own the negotiation.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The Cadence conversion clock:** Huntington closed its Cadence systems conversion two hundred thirty-five days after announcement and is targeting three hundred sixty-five million dollars in synergies by Q4. If your client is in the middle of an integration, what does their day-count look like, and is their finance function tracking against a comparably explicit synergy realization schedule?
2. **The tariff chapter in your scenario library:** Section one-twenty-two expired today. If a client's Q3 planning cycle uses a tariff scenario that was calibrated before today, it is already stale. When did they last refresh the credit and macro stress assumptions that drive their loan-loss provisioning models?
3. **The FSB governance benchmark for agentic AI:** The FSB comment period on agentic AI governance closed two days ago. The final report goes to G20 finance ministers in October. Does your client's CFO know whether their agentic AI pilots in treasury or close automation meet the FSB's "dual authorization for agents executing financial transactions above threshold" standard -- and if not, who owns the remediation?

item.title: Finance Pulse - Jul 23, 2026
item.description:
## Finance Pulse | Thursday, July 23, 2026
**Bottom line: With Q2 earnings season fully closed, the finance function agenda pivots sharply: deposit mix is quietly improving across the industry in ways that change NII planning assumptions, the bank M&A machine is running at a seven-year high and generating system-integration demand that finance teams cannot ignore, and the OneStream Finance Agentic Layer release signals that EPM vendor competition for the bank CFO's AI budget is now the defining procurement battleground of the second half.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. Bank M&A transaction volume hit fifteen point one billion dollars in the first six months of 2026, its highest level in seven years, and the integration workload that follows is the most underappreciated driver of finance transformation spending right now. 2. BankUnited reported Q2 non-interest-bearing deposits reaching thirty-four point four percent of total deposits, an all-time high that exceeded even the COVID-era peak, a deposit-mix signal CFOs across the industry should build into second-half NII models. 3. OneStream announced at its Splash User Conference the general availability of SensibleAI Agents and a Finance Agentic Layer that uses open Model Context Protocol to give any AI tool secure, governed access to OneStream data with full auditability and permissions trails, a direct move to capture bank finance-function AI spend. 4. The March 2026 Basel III Endgame re-proposal delivers net capital relief of approximately eighty-seven point seven billion dollars versus the original twenty-nineteen capital increase, with finalization expected in late 2026 and implementation in 2027; the comment period has closed and the clock to final rule is running. 5. With geopolitical uncertainty reduced, experts say larger bank M&A could accelerate, and more regional banks may pursue merger opportunities to address scale and technology challenges.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): Deposit Mix Recovery as a Planning Variable** At BankUnited, deposit growth helped lift profitability: total deposits excluding brokered deposits rose one point one billion dollars, net interest margin improved to three point zero six percent, and average deposit costs declined as the bank reduced reliance on higher-cost wholesale funding. This is the new story post-earnings season: NIB deposit recovery is no longer just a mega-bank phenomenon. Across the Q2 reporting cycle, PNC's average noninterest-bearing balances grew four percent linked quarter to one hundred three point five billion dollars, representing twenty-three percent of total average deposits, with NII rising four percent to four point one billion dollars. For CFOs, the planning implication is asymmetric: if NIB mix continues recovering while rates hold flat, deposit beta improvements compound into NII upside that current consensus models may underweight.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): M&A Integration as Finance Transformation Catalyst** Large transactions continue to drive banking M&A value, with PwC's 2026 midyear banking deals outlook counting five U.S. banking transactions above five billion dollars in the most recent four-quarter period; beneath those headline deals, more than one hundred thirty bank-to-bank transactions and approximately one hundred credit union mergers show that consolidation is continuing across regional and community banking. The finance transformation demand signal is specific: super-regional banks are well positioned to drive the next wave of consolidation, and as technology investment grows more expensive, scale offers a way to spread costs and strengthen competitive positioning. Every completed deal creates a general ledger rationalization, a chart-of-accounts harmonization, and a planning-tool consolidation project. Santander's twelve point two billion dollar agreement to acquire Webster Financial adds a cross-border ERP and regulatory reporting dimension that amplifies the complexity.
**Theme 3 (New): EPM Vendor AI Arms Race Reaches Decision Moment** The finance technology vendor landscape has moved from AI roadmap positioning to shipping product. OneStream's Finance Agentic Layer uses open Model Context Protocol to give any AI tool secure, governed access to OneStream data with the financial logic, auditability, and permissions and audit trails that finance requires, with management noting that generic tools operate without the financial context, logic, and governance required for financial decision-making. Separately, in 2026 Workday has invested heavily in Illuminate, its next-generation AI layer, which extends across planning, reporting, reconciliation, and expense management with agentic AI capabilities that can take multi-step actions on behalf of finance users. And Oracle Financial Services has introduced an enterprise-class suite of AI-infused applications, design tools, frameworks, and pre-built AI agents specifically targeted at banks. The CFO now has competing agentic-AI pitches from every major EPM vendor simultaneously, making governance and ROI frameworks the deciding factor, not feature comparisons.
---
### Banking Finance-Function
**NIM and NII:** PNC's NIM expanded one basis point to two point nine six percent, reflecting lower rates paid on interest-bearing deposits partially offset by a shift toward lower-spread, high-credit-quality loans. At the community bank level, Preferred Bank has one point five billion dollars in CDs maturing in Q3 at an average rate of three point eight zero percent, and those will likely come back on at a slightly higher rate, flagging a CD repricing headwind that affects NIM guidance for asset-sensitive institutions. First BanCorp guided to three to five basis points of NIM expansion per quarter for the remainder of 2026, assuming interest rates remain stable.
**Capital Returns:** PNC's ROTCE was seventeen point nine percent for Q2, the company returned one point three billion dollars to shareholders through dividends and buybacks, and the board approved an eighteen percent increase to the quarterly common stock dividend, raising the payout by thirty cents to two dollars per share.
**Credit:** Preferred Bank significantly reduced non-performing and criticized loans by seventy million dollars, a forty-one point five percent reduction, and criticized loans by ninety million dollars, a thirty-four percent reduction, lowering reserve requirements and reducing provision expenses to one point two million dollars.
**M&A Signal for Finance Functions:** Regions Financial acquired Frazier Lanier Company, an investment bank specializing in municipal and corporate securities, which will be integrated into Regions' capital markets division. This is a capability-buy, not a balance sheet buy, and it creates new revenue-line reporting and transfer-pricing complexity for the controller and FP&A team.
---
### Regulatory Radar
On March nineteenth, U.S. regulators released the Basel III Endgame re-proposal, moving from internal models to new standardized approaches for credit and operational risk; the consultation period ended June eighteenth, 2026. The post-comment finalization window is the current state. The Federal Reserve, OCC, and FDIC now project that aggregate capital will modestly decrease under the new framework, a dramatic pivot from the original plus-sixteen-percent CET1 proposal; but for operational risk managers, the structural change remains significant: internal models are still eliminated, the Standardized Approach is still coming, and the compliance clock is ticking. The shift from Advanced Measurement Approach to Standardized Approach is not a compliance checkbox: it transforms how loss data is collected, validated, and reported, which is a direct finance-function data infrastructure investment. Finalization is expected in Q4 2026, with implementation beginning in 2027.
---
### AI in Finance
**What is actually shipping:** OneStream announced the general availability of SensibleAI Agents, pre-built agents operating natively on the OneStream platform and integrated into Microsoft Office 365, alongside a Finance Agentic Layer that opens those capabilities to third-party AI tools for forecasting, guiding, and reporting using Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini.
**CFO Agenda Connection:** The governance angle is the critical differentiator from generic AI tools. The Finance Agentic Layer uses open Model Context Protocol to give any AI tool secure, governed access to OneStream data with the financial logic, auditability, and permissions and audit trails that finance requires. For a bank CFO, this is the specific capability that converts AI from a productivity curiosity into a defensible control environment. Oracle's pitch is similar but bank-specific: the Application Tracker agent delivers proactive management by predicting delays and recommending next steps in loan origination, while the Qualitative Analysis and Credit Decisioning agent intelligently suggests responses for complex scorecards, resulting in faster and more consistent credit decisions.
**Reality Check vs. Hype:** According to the June 2025 General Atlantic AI Survey, finance and accounting is the lowest-ranked function for AI deployment across all business departments, with full workflow automation and agents already mainstream in engineering, marketing, and customer success, while finance is not there yet. The adoption gap is compounded by execution failure: eighty-four percent of organizations have deployed AI without redesigning jobs, creating the exact problem of technology deployed, adoption low, impact minimal.
**Buying Patterns:** Fifty percent of North American CFOs say digital transformation of finance is their top priority for 2026, and eighty-seven percent expect AI to be extremely or very important to their finance department's operations. Deloitte's Finance Trends 2026 research shows most finance departments piloting AI use cases, with sixty-three percent actively using AI solutions. The budget is moving; the ROI evidence is still accumulating.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The post-earnings season creates a distinct planning window. Three forces are converging simultaneously for bank CFOs: a flat-rate environment that makes deposit-mix management the primary NII lever, a Basel finalization timeline that requires data infrastructure investment regardless of the capital outcome, and an EPM vendor market that is now shipping agentic AI product at scale and demanding a procurement decision.
The M&A integration workload is the underappreciated finance transformation driver. Prosperity Bancshares' integration of Stellar Bancorp is currently scheduled for March 2027, illustrating the multi-quarter systems harmonization timeline that finance transformation consultants should anchor client conversations around. Buyers are using M&A to gain scale in priority markets, add specialty business lines, accelerate technology and talent acquisition, and rationalize overlapping branch networks, and every one of those objectives lands in the finance function's lap as a data, reporting, or planning challenge.
More regional banks may pursue merger opportunities in order to address scale and technology challenges, suggesting the pipeline of integration-driven finance transformation engagements is not thinning in the second half of 2026.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The entire AI-in-finance conversation is vendor-supply-driven, not client-demand-driven. Every major EPM platform is shipping agentic AI simultaneously, which means the constraint is not product availability but bank finance team capacity and governance readiness to absorb it. The sixty-three percent of finance departments piloting AI coexists with eighty-four percent of organizations that deployed AI without redesigning jobs and got minimal impact. The CFO's real investment priority for the second half is not another AI tool license but the change management and governance infrastructure to make the tools already purchased produce results. Consultants who lead with technology selection are solving last year's problem.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **Deposit mix recovery as an NII planning assumption:** BankUnited's NIB deposits hit an all-time high of thirty-four point four percent of total deposits in Q2. Is your client's second-half NII forecast building in the deposit-mix tailwind, or is it anchored to a conservative beta assumption that no longer reflects current behavior?
2. **Basel operational risk data infrastructure:** The shift from internal AMA models to the Standardized Approach under the Basel III re-proposal eliminates model development work but creates new loss-data quality and Business Indicator calculation requirements. Has your client scoped the data infrastructure investment needed before the Q4 2026 finalization, or are they waiting for a final rule before acting?
3. **M&A integration as the finance transformation entry point:** Bank M&A volume is at a seven-year high and every completed deal generates an immediate general ledger, planning tool, and regulatory reporting rationalization project. Which of your super-regional clients is currently in a post-close integration phase, and is that the front door to a broader finance transformation conversation?

1. OneStream announced at its Splash User Conference the general availability of SensibleAI Agents and a Finance Agentic Layer that uses open Model Context Protocol to give any AI tool secure, governed access to OneStream data with full auditability and permissions trails, a direct move to capture bank finance-function AI spend. 4. The March 2026 Basel III Endgame re-proposal delivers net capital relief of approximately eighty-seven point seven billion dollars versus the original twenty-nineteen capital increase, with finalization expected in late 2026 and implementation in 2027; the comment period has closed and the clock to final rule is running. 5. With geopolitical uncertainty reduced, experts say larger bank M&A could accelerate, and more regional banks may pursue merger opportunities to address scale and technology challenges.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): Deposit Mix Recovery as a Planning Variable** At BankUnited, deposit growth helped lift profitability: total deposits excluding brokered deposits rose one point one billion dollars, net interest margin improved to three point zero six percent, and average deposit costs declined as the bank reduced reliance on higher-cost wholesale funding. This is the new story post-earnings season: NIB deposit recovery is no longer just a mega-bank phenomenon. Across the Q2 reporting cycle, PNC's average noninterest-bearing balances grew four percent linked quarter to one hundred three point five billion dollars, representing twenty-three percent of total average deposits, with NII rising four percent to four point one billion dollars. For CFOs, the planning implication is asymmetric: if NIB mix continues recovering while rates hold flat, deposit beta improvements compound into NII upside that current consensus models may underweight.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): M&A Integration as Finance Transformation Catalyst** Large transactions continue to drive banking M&A value, with PwC's 2026 midyear banking deals outlook counting five U.S. banking transactions above five billion dollars in the most recent four-quarter period; beneath those headline deals, more than one hundred thirty bank-to-bank transactions and approximately one hundred credit union mergers show that consolidation is continuing across regional and community banking. The finance transformation demand signal is specific: super-regional banks are well positioned to drive the next wave of consolidation, and as technology investment grows more expensive, scale offers a way to spread costs and strengthen competitive positioning. Separately, in 2026 Workday has invested heavily in Illuminate, its next-generation AI layer, which extends across planning, reporting, reconciliation, and expense management with agentic AI capabilities that can take multi-step actions on behalf of finance users. **NIM and NII:** PNC's NIM expanded one basis point to two point nine six percent, reflecting lower rates paid on interest-bearing deposits partially offset by a shift toward lower-spread, high-credit-quality loans. ## Finance Pulse | Wednesday, July 22, 2026
**Bottom line: KeyCorp's Q2 beat closes the super-regional earnings cycle on a bullish note, but the real story now shifts to post-earnings planning: a hawkish-hold Fed seven days out, a Basel III re-proposal in its final comment-digestion window, and a measurable CFO consensus that agentic AI has crossed from pilot to execution priority.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. KeyCorp delivered Q2 GAAP net income of four hundred seventy-two million dollars, or forty-four cents per diluted share, a twenty-two percent increase in net income and a twenty-six percent EPS gain versus Q2 2025. The print closes the super-regional earnings season. 2. At the July twenty-eight to twenty-nine FOMC meeting, policymakers are expected to leave rates unchanged while preserving the option to tighten further if inflation proves persistent. The rate-path uncertainty is the single most important planning variable for bank CFOs heading into H2. 3. Deloitte's CFO Signals survey found fifty percent of large-company CFOs named digital finance transformation their top 2026 priority, and eighty-seven percent believe AI will be extremely or very important to how their finance department operates this year.
---
### Three Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): KeyCorp's guidance raise reframes the super-regional NII arc**
KeyCorp raised several full-year 2026 guidance metrics: the bank now expects revenue to grow seven to eight percent versus prior guidance of approximately seven percent, full-year net interest income to increase nine to eleven percent versus the prior range of nine to ten percent, and average loan growth of four to five percent, up from two to four percent, with average commercial loans now expected to rise eight to ten percent for the year.
The bank's net interest margin expanded sequentially to two point eight nine percent, with management saying KeyCorp remains on track to meet or exceed a three percent margin by year-end. Notably, M&A pipelines rose seven percent to a record level, and the bank expects third-quarter investment banking fees to be up more than twenty percent sequentially. The implication for the cohort: commercial loan demand is durable enough to sustain NII guidance lifts even without rate cuts, as long as C&I utilization holds.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): The Fed's hawkish-hold posture reshapes CFO planning horizons**
The June sixteen to seventeen FOMC meeting, the first chaired by Kevin Warsh, resulted in a unanimous decision to keep rates unchanged at three point fifty to three point seventy-five percent, with the statement highlighting solid economic growth and persistent inflation above the two percent target. Markets currently assign approximately twenty-five percent probability to a twenty-five basis point rate hike at the July twenty-eight to twenty-nine meeting; Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signaled that inflation is now the primary policy concern, with risks "completely flipped" from labor market weakness to price stability. Futures markets price a path that rises to about three point eight percent by October 2026 and approaches four percent around year-end. For bank CFOs, this is a markedly different planning scenario than the cut cycle embedded in most 2026 budget models: asset-sensitive balance sheets now face a potential upside scenario, but deposit repricing risk is not zero.
**Theme 3 (Evolving): Basel III re-proposal enters its critical finalization window**
The July 2023 proposal sought a roughly nineteen percent capital increase for the largest US banks; the March 2026 re-proposal instead delivers net capital relief of about eighty-seven point seven billion dollars, with finalization expected in late 2026 and implementation in 2027. Reductions run to approximately four point eight percent for the G-SIBs, five point two percent for large regionals, and seven point eight percent for smaller institutions. Comments on the proposals were due June eighteenth, 2026. The agencies are now processing comment letters, and finalization before year-end would require banks to begin implementation planning immediately. For finance transformation leaders, the capital relief creates a new question: does freed CET1 capacity get redeployed into technology investment, buybacks, or loan growth?
---
### Banking Finance-Function
**NIM and NII:** KeyCorp's net interest margin improved to two point eight nine percent, with a sequential rise in commercial and industrial loans by two point one billion dollars, or three percent. M&T Bank guided full-year NIM in the high three point sixty percent range with NII in the lower half of the seven point two billion to seven point thirty-five billion dollar range.
**Deposit beta stabilization:** M&T's cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta guidance is in the low to mid fifty percent range. M&T's interest-bearing deposit costs decreased only slightly, by two basis points, to one point ninety-five percent, indicating ongoing but decelerating pressure on deposit pricing.
**Efficiency and operating leverage:** KeyCorp's cash efficiency ratio came in at sixty-one point nine percent versus the analyst estimate of sixty-two point one percent. Gorman said the bank expects revenue to grow about twice as fast as expenses in 2026, producing substantial positive operating leverage.
**Capital:** KeyCorp's Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio held at twelve point eight percent. The bank repurchased over three hundred forty million dollars in common stock, targeting at least one point three billion for the full year.
**Fee income as structural diversifier:** Investment banking, commercial payments, and wealth collectively grew eight percent in the first half of 2026 versus the first half of 2025, with investment banking and debt placement fees totaling one hundred sixty-nine million dollars in the second quarter.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III re-proposal (post-comment period):** The June eighteenth comment deadline has passed. The 2026 proposals are intended to streamline capital requirements and better align regulatory capital with risk, with agencies anticipating that the amount of overall capital in the banking system "would modestly decrease" if the proposals are implemented. The re-proposal also eliminates the requirement to deduct mortgage servicing rights from regulatory capital, designed to pull mortgage activity back onto bank balance sheets, and replaces the dual-ratio system with a single Expanded Risk-Based Approach. For finance transformation teams, the shift from dual-ratio to single Expanded Risk-Based Approach has direct implications for RWA calculation infrastructure and regulatory reporting architecture.
**FOMC (July twenty-eight to twenty-nine):** One week out. No SEP will be produced at this meeting, per prior communications. There is not a Summary of Economic Projections that will be produced for that meeting. All signal will come from the statement language and Chair Warsh's press conference.
---
### AI in Finance
**The agentic AI signal is getting specific, not just broad.** Fifty-four percent of surveyed CFOs named integrating AI agents into finance workflows as a top transformation priority, ahead of improving data quality, access, and usability at fifty-two percent; Deloitte's Steve Gallucci described the shift as finance leaders moving "from exploration to execution" on technology.
**What banks are actually buying:** KeyCorp management is deploying about one billion dollars into technology and AI for better products and efficiency in 2026, one of the clearest named-dollar commitments from a super-regional this cycle. Technology investments include a focus on wealth platforms, APIs, and AI applications. This signals that for mid-tier banks, the technology budget is not a cost-cutting story but a growth-enabling one: fee income diversification into wealth, payments, and investment banking all require platform investment.
**The sequencing imperative:** Bain's 2026 finance transformation guidance notes that AI-first finance transformation requires deliberate sequencing: data foundation first, automation second, intelligence third, with CFOs who invest in AI before fixing data quality getting poor results. For bank finance teams still running fragmented general ledger environments or multi-ERP landscapes, this sequencing argument is the consultative entry point.
**Human plus agent model:** In 2026, leading finance departments function as human-plus-agent collaboratives, where AI agents handle data-intensive routine tasks such as reconciliations, invoice processing, and outlier detection, while humans focus on interpretation of anomalies, scenario evaluation, and strategic business partnering, freeing finance teams to move from data wrangling toward actionable foresight at scale.
**Governance and ROI realism:** The evidence shows real gains in automation of routine finance tasks, enhanced forecasting, and stronger fraud defenses, yet CFOs rightly recognize the limits: data issues, ethical concerns, and a need for sustained, not instant, ROI. Banks deploying AI in regulatory reporting and stress testing face the added dimension of model risk governance overlaying the AI governance layer, a dual burden most vendors do not yet fully address.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The guidance-raising environment changes the FP&A workload calculus.** With KeyCorp raising NII guidance to nine to eleven percent and loan growth to four to five percent mid-cycle, FP&A teams are now running re-forecast cycles faster than their annual planning cadence was designed to support. The demand for rolling forecasts and continuous planning platforms is a direct output of a volatile-but-upward rate and volume environment.
**Technology spend as a distinct earnings call narrative.** KeyCorp's one-billion-dollar technology commitment and M&T's investment-in-efficiency framing suggest that bank CFOs are increasingly using technology investment as an investor relations lever, not just an internal efficiency story. Finance transformation leaders should treat the CFO's earnings call language as a leading indicator of where budget authority is moving.
**Middle-market investment banking lag is a data point for finance modeling.** Gorman acknowledged that middle-market M&A activity has lagged larger transactions, noting that forty percent of KeyCorp's investment banking fees are driven by private equity. When private equity dealmaking is bifurcated from broader M&A, fee revenue planning models must disaggregate sponsor-driven versus corporate-driven pipelines, a FP&A complexity challenge that most regional banks have not fully embedded in their driver-based models.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The prevailing narrative after the super-regional earnings season is that NIM expansion vindicates the higher-for-longer rate environment. But the more precise read is that NIM expansion has been driven largely by asset repricing and loan mix shifts, not by deposit cost compression. Interest-bearing deposit costs at M&T decreased only two basis points to one point ninety-five percent, and with markets currently assigning approximately twenty-five percent probability to a hike at the July meeting, the next leg of NIM expansion depends on whether the rate path moves up or whether repricing tailwinds fade. CFOs who are modeling NIM expansion as a durable trend without stress-testing a flat-or-down deposit cost scenario are carrying more forecast risk than they may realize. The finance transformation imperative here is not AI; it is better deposit-pricing analytics and liability-side scenario modeling.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The guidance-raise question:** KeyCorp lifted NII guidance to nine to eleven percent mid-cycle and loan growth to four to five percent. How frequently is your FP&A team running re-forecasts, and does your planning platform support in-cycle guidance revision without a full re-budget cycle?
2. **Basel III capital relief and redeployment:** With the March 2026 re-proposal delivering net CET1 relief, the capital allocation conversation for CFOs has changed. Is your capital planning model already reflecting the reduced-stringency scenario, and has your finance team mapped how freed capital flows into technology, buybacks, or loan growth decisions?
3. **The agentic AI sequencing test:** Deloitte and Bain both flag data quality as the prerequisite for AI value. Before your bank invests in agentic FP&A or automated regulatory reporting, does the CFO have an honest assessment of whether the data foundation, specifically GL integrity, entity hierarchies, and cost center governance, is actually AI-ready?

**The agentic AI signal is getting specific, not just broad.** Fifty-four percent of surveyed CFOs named integrating AI agents into finance workflows as a top transformation priority, ahead of improving data quality, access, and usability at fifty-two percent; Deloitte's Steve Gallucci described the shift as finance leaders moving "from exploration to execution" on technology.
**What banks are actually buying:** KeyCorp management is deploying about one billion dollars into technology and AI for better products and efficiency in 2026, one of the clearest named-dollar commitments from a super-regional this cycle. Technology investments include a focus on wealth platforms, APIs, and AI applications. This signals that for mid-tier banks, the technology budget is not a cost-cutting story but a growth-enabling one: fee income diversification into wealth, payments, and investment banking all require platform investment.
**The sequencing imperative:** Bain's 2026 finance transformation guidance notes that AI-first finance transformation requires deliberate sequencing: data foundation first, automation second, intelligence third, with CFOs who invest in AI before fixing data quality getting poor results. For bank finance teams still running fragmented general ledger environments or multi-ERP landscapes, this sequencing argument is the consultative entry point.
**Human plus agent model:** In 2026, leading finance departments function as human-plus-agent collaboratives, where AI agents handle data-intensive routine tasks such as reconciliations, invoice processing, and outlier detection, while humans focus on interpretation of anomalies, scenario evaluation, and strategic business partnering, freeing finance teams to move from data wrangling toward actionable foresight at scale.
**Governance and ROI realism:** The evidence shows real gains in automation of routine finance tasks, enhanced forecasting, and stronger fraud defenses, yet CFOs rightly recognize the limits: data issues, ethical concerns, and a need for sustained, not instant, ROI. Banks deploying AI in regulatory reporting and stress testing face the added dimension of model risk governance overlaying the AI governance layer, a dual burden most vendors do not yet fully address.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The guidance-raising environment changes the FP&A workload calculus.** With KeyCorp raising NII guidance to nine to eleven percent and loan growth to four to five percent mid-cycle, FP&A teams are now running re-forecast cycles faster than their annual planning cadence was designed to support. The demand for rolling forecasts and continuous planning platforms is a direct output of a volatile-but-upward rate and volume environment.
**Technology spend as a distinct earnings call narrative.** KeyCorp's one-billion-dollar technology commitment and M&T's investment-in-efficiency framing suggest that bank CFOs are increasingly using technology investment as an investor relations lever, not just an internal efficiency story. Finance transformation leaders should treat the CFO's earnings call language as a leading indicator of where budget authority is moving.
**Middle-market investment banking lag is a data point for finance modeling.** Gorman acknowledged that middle-market M&A activity has lagged larger transactions, noting that forty percent of KeyCorp's investment banking fees are driven by private equity. When private equity dealmaking is bifurcated from broader M&A, fee revenue planning models must disaggregate sponsor-driven versus corporate-driven pipelines, a FP&A complexity challenge that most regional banks have not fully embedded in their driver-based models.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The prevailing narrative after the super-regional earnings season is that NIM expansion vindicates the higher-for-longer rate environment. But the more precise read is that NIM expansion has been driven largely by asset repricing and loan mix shifts, not by deposit cost compression. Interest-bearing deposit costs at M&T decreased only two basis points to one point ninety-five percent, and with markets currently assigning approximately twenty-five percent probability to a hike at the July meeting, the next leg of NIM expansion depends on whether the rate path moves up or whether repricing tailwinds fade. CFOs who are modeling NIM expansion as a durable trend without stress-testing a flat-or-down deposit cost scenario are carrying more forecast risk than they may realize. The finance transformation imperative here is not AI; it is better deposit-pricing analytics and liability-side scenario modeling.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The guidance-raise question:** KeyCorp lifted NII guidance to nine to eleven percent mid-cycle and loan growth to four to five percent. How frequently is your FP&A team running re-forecasts, and does your planning platform support in-cycle guidance revision without a full re-budget cycle?
2. **Basel III capital relief and redeployment:** With the March 2026 re-proposal delivering net CET1 relief, the capital allocation conversation for CFOs has changed. Is your capital planning model already reflecting the reduced-stringency scenario, and has your finance team mapped how freed capital flows into technology, buybacks, or loan growth decisions?
3. **The agentic AI sequencing test:** Deloitte and Bain both flag data quality as the prerequisite for AI value. Before your bank invests in agentic FP&A or automated regulatory reporting, does the CFO have an honest assessment of whether the data foundation, specifically GL integrity, entity hierarchies, and cost center governance, is actually AI-ready?

item.title: Finance Pulse - Jul 21, 2026
item.description:
I now have sufficient data across all coverage areas to build today's briefing. Note: KeyCorp's actual Q2 results were not yet published in search results (the call is at 9 AM ET today, July 21), so I will report the pre-print consensus and known context, and flag it as a live print morning. The AlphaStreet ticker confirms the print is this morning. I also have the AlphaStreet ticker confirming Truist delivered a 12.8% upside and Fifth Third posted a 46% revenue jump, which are today's fresh data points. Let me now build both parts.
---
## Finance Pulse | Tuesday, July 21, 2026
**Bottom line: KeyCorp's Q2 print lands this morning, closing the super-regional earnings season; simultaneously, the Fed's July 29 FOMC is one week out with a hike option still on the table, the Basel III re-proposal is now in the post-comment finalization window, and agentic AI is moving from boardroom promise to budget line -- with the data sequencing problem emerging as the single biggest barrier between banks and real ROI.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. KeyCorp reports Q2 this morning before the bell; consensus is forty-two cents per share on one point nine eight billion in revenue, up twenty percent year over year on EPS and eight percent on revenue. The bank has consistently surpassed Wall Street EPS estimates in its last four quarterly reports, making a beat the base case -- but the NIM trajectory and updated NII guidance are the numbers the finance community will use to close out the cohort read.
2. Markets currently assign approximately twenty-five percent probability to a twenty-five basis point rate hike at the July twenty-eight to twenty-nine FOMC meeting. Policymakers are expected to leave rates unchanged while preserving the option to tighten further if inflation proves persistent. That optionality creates genuine planning uncertainty for bank CFOs.
3. Most finance organizations have still not turned AI potential into measurable impact. BCG's AI Radar 2026 found that spending on AI is set to double as a share of revenue, and ninety-four percent of organizations plan to continue investing despite uncertain short-term returns.
---
### Three Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): KeyCorp as the Cohort Capstone**
The consensus EPS of forty-two cents represents a twenty percent increase from the thirty-five cents KeyCorp earned in Q2 2025, while the revenue consensus of one point nine seven billion implies seven point one percent growth from year-ago revenue of one point eight four billion. C&I loans account for roughly fifty percent of KeyCorp's average loan balances, and demand was robust in Q2 -- making the commercial lending color particularly relevant for the cohort. Notably, analyst sentiment deteriorated modestly heading into the print, setting a lower bar and increasing beat probability. Management has flagged deployment of about one billion dollars into technology and AI for better products and efficiency, which makes today's call a live read on how super-regionals are narrating AI investment ROI to investors.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): Rate Uncertainty Stiffens CFO Planning**
The FOMC held the federal funds rate target at three and a half to three and three-quarter percent at its June meeting. Under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's leadership, the FOMC adopted a notably more hawkish tone; the median federal funds rate projection for 2026 was revised upward from three point four percent to three point eight percent, while the PCE inflation forecast jumped from two point seven to three point six percent. The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for July twenty-eight and twenty-nine, with no Summary of Economic Projections produced for that meeting. The absence of a dot plot at this meeting means CFOs get a binary yes/no on rates with no updated forward guidance to anchor their second-half planning.
**Theme 3 (New): Basel III Comment Period Closed -- Finalization Clock Running**
On March nineteenth, 2026, the Federal Reserve, OCC, and FDIC issued three proposals that would comprehensively overhaul the existing U.S. bank capital framework. The comment period on the 2026 re-proposal closed on June eighteenth, 2026. Regulators will issue a final rule thereafter, with phased implementation expected between 2027 and 2028. The March 2026 re-proposal delivers net capital relief of about eighty-seven point seven billion dollars, with finalization expected in late 2026 and implementation in 2027. The direction is capital neutral to slightly relieving -- but internal models are still gone, the Standardized Approach is still coming, and the compliance clock is ticking regardless of headline capital impact.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**Cohort Earnings Wrap:** The AlphaStreet ticker this morning confirms Truist Financial delivered a twelve point eight percent Q2 2026 upside with revenue up six percent, and Fifth Third Bancorp posted a forty-six percent revenue jump in Q2 2026, beating on EPS. These are the last pre-KeyCorp data points. There has been positive sentiment among investors in the regional banks segment, with share prices up six point three percent on average over the last month.
**NIM and NII:** Stabilizing funding and deposit costs, combined with a solid lending scenario and decent economic growth, are expected to have supported KeyCorp's NII in Q2. The Fed pause -- with a hike optionality -- creates an unusual NIM planning environment: further cuts are off the table, a hike would temporarily widen asset yields but reprice deposit bases faster than many CFOs assumed in 2025 models.
**Credit and Provisioning:** M&T Bank delivered year-on-year revenue growth of five point five percent, beating analysts' expectations by two point five percent, continuing its nine-consecutive-quarter credit quality improvement arc. Regional bank shares are up six point three percent on average over the last month, suggesting markets are pricing benign credit into the sector broadly.
**Capital:** The agencies anticipate that the amount of overall capital in the banking system would modestly decrease if the re-proposals are implemented. The FRB voted six to one to advance all three proposals, with Governor Michael Barr as the sole dissenting vote, signaling bipartisan regulatory alignment for a capital-neutral framework.
---
### Regulatory Radar
Basel III is now the most time-sensitive item on the finance transformation agenda. Large banks should plan for a twelve to eighteen month implementation window from final-rule issuance. Banks investing in data foundations, automation, and flexible platforms win regardless of final calibration. The operational risk change is particularly underappreciated: the Standardized Approach eliminates the need for model development and validation but introduces new requirements around loss data quality and Business Indicator calculation, which is a direct demand signal for data platform investment.
For super-regionals, extending the frameworks to banks with assets between one hundred billion and seven hundred billion dollars raised questions about proportionality -- and those Category III and IV institutions are now building compliance programs with still-uncertain scope parameters. That uncertainty is itself a transformation driver.
---
### AI in Finance
The sequencing problem is the story right now. AI-first finance transformation requires deliberate sequencing: data foundation first, automation second, intelligence third. CFOs who invest in AI before fixing data quality get poor results; those who sequence correctly get compounding returns.
AI capabilities are increasingly moving from prototype to product -- but it is also clear that most finance organizations still have not turned that potential into measurable impact. This gap between adoption and impact is now the primary question in client conversations, and it maps directly to where banks are actually spending.
On agentic AI specifically: early agentic AI use cases have shown significant potential, enabling zero-touch operations and reducing manual workloads by thirty to fifty percent; in 2025 alone, fifty of the world's largest banks announced more than one hundred sixty use cases. The next threshold is moving from announcement to measured production deployment.
Continuous assurance transforms the audit model from sampling-based to one hundred percent transaction monitoring, and agentic AI dramatically compresses cycle times by eliminating human latency between insight and action. For bank controllers and internal audit functions, this is the most concrete near-term ROI case.
**CFO budget signals:** CFOs are dedicating approximately twenty-five percent of their budgets to AI agents and anticipating roughly twenty percent lifts in revenue or cost savings. Deloitte's Finance Trends 2026 research shows most finance departments piloting AI use cases, with sixty-three percent actively using AI solutions. The pilot-to-production conversion rate, not the adoption headline, is what finance transformation consultants should pressure-test with clients.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The simultaneous arrival of three forces -- the post-comment Basel finalization clock, the FOMC hike optionality in eight days, and the close of super-regional Q2 earnings -- creates a compressed planning window for bank CFOs. Updated capital modeling, NII scenario rebasing, and regulatory data readiness are all live workstreams right now.
Recent 2026 benchmarks reveal a radical shift in how top-tier finance teams operate: eighty-two percent of midsize companies have begun implementing AI agents that autonomously manage cash flow fluctuations and predict working capital needs. Banks are behind that curve in controlled deployments, constrained by model risk governance, SR 11-7 obligations, and data quality gaps.
Visionaries anticipate the rise of the "ten times bank," where a single individual leads a team of AI co-workers to deliver exponentially greater output. In this model, growth is no longer constrained by headcount; instead, success depends on an organization's ability to reinvent work and shape a human-and-agent workforce. For finance transformation consultants, this framing -- the human-and-agent workforce -- is where the operating model conversation needs to land.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The super-regional Q2 earnings season has been broadly positive, but the NIM tailwind story may be masking an underappreciated planning risk: a Fed hike at July twenty-nine would widen short-end asset yields quickly, but super-regionals with large proportions of fixed-rate loan books and already-repriced deposit bases would see funding cost acceleration outpace asset repricing for one to two quarters. The banks that beat on NII guidance this quarter are the ones most exposed if Warsh moves. CFOs anchoring second-half NII guidance on rate-hold assumptions should be stress-testing that scenario explicitly -- and most earnings call transcripts suggest they are not.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **Basel data readiness vs. capital neutrality confusion:** Most super-regional finance teams are reading the "capital neutral" headline and relaxing their Basel preparation timelines. The Standardized Approach's loss data quality requirements and Business Indicator calculations represent a genuine data infrastructure build regardless of aggregate capital impact. Are your clients' data programs scoped to the operational requirements, not just the capital number?
2. **KeyCorp's AI investment narrative as a template:** Today's earnings call at nine AM ET is the first place management will publicly narrate a one-billion-dollar technology and AI investment commitment to analysts. How management connects that spend to efficiency ratio improvement and NIM protection will set the template for how the cohort tells the AI investment story through the rest of 2026. What are your clients' boards asking them to demonstrate in return?
3. **The data-sequencing problem as a gateway conversation:** Sixty-three percent of finance organizations are actively using AI, but BCG finds most have not converted that into measurable impact. The reason is almost always sequencing: AI deployed before data quality is resolved produces unreliable results. This is the single most actionable entry point for a finance transformation conversation at a bank right now -- not "do you have an AI strategy" but "have you fixed your data foundation first?"

item.title: Finance Pulse - Jul 20, 2026
item.description:
I now have comprehensive data across all coverage areas. Let me note what's genuinely new for Monday, July 20: (1) KeyCorp reports Q2 tomorrow morning (July 21) -- this is a live pre-earnings moment for the last major super-regional in the cohort; (2) Truist and Fifth Third both delivered Q2 beats that cleared the wire this morning per the AlphaStreet ticker; (3) Regions' deposit cost number (one point six nine percent, down three basis points) is fresh post-print color; (4) Basel III comment period closed June 18 -- we are now squarely in the post-comment, pre-finalization window with Q4 2026 finalization expected; (5) the Bank of America Q2 deposit mix deterioration (NIBs falling, shift to CDs/money markets) is a distinct deposit economics angle not previously covered; (6) Bloomberg Intelligence's two hundred thousand job projection from AI is a specific new workforce data point; (7) the June CPI at three point five percent year-over-year is freshly confirmed; (8) the July twenty-nine FOMC is nine days away, with futures implying a hike probability that has eased back. Let me now construct both outputs.
---
## Finance Pulse | Monday, July 20, 2026
**Bottom line: With the June eighteen Basel comment window now closed and finalization tracking for Q4 2026, every super-regional CFO faces a concrete 12-to-18-month implementation clock -- and the post-comment silence is itself a planning signal that finance transformation budgets cannot ignore.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. The comment period on the 2026 Basel III re-proposal closed June 18, 2026. Regulators will issue a final rule thereafter, with phased implementation expected between 2027 and 2028. The post-comment window is where regulatory modeling and data infrastructure work must begin in earnest -- waiting for a final rule is no longer a defensible posture.
2. KeyCorp reports Q2 2026 results tomorrow, July 21, before the opening bell, with analyst consensus calling for earnings of zero dollars and forty-two cents per share on revenue of one point nine seven billion dollars. It is the last major super-regional print of the cycle and the most watched NIM recovery story in the cohort.
3. The June CPI report showed headline inflation easing to three point five percent year over year -- down sharply from May's four point two percent -- while core CPI slowed to two point six percent. That softer print, alongside the May PCE report putting core PCE at three point four percent, hands the Committee its first clear disinflation signal in months.
4. At the FOMC's July 28 to 29, 2026 meeting, policymakers are expected to leave rates unchanged while preserving the option to tighten further if inflation proves persistent.
5. Regions Financial posted NII of one point two eight billion dollars, supported by a net interest margin of three point six six percent and interest-bearing deposit costs of one point six nine percent, with average loans up two percent to ninety-eight point seven billion dollars driven by commercial and industrial growth.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The Post-Comment Basel Window Is the New Action Horizon**
The June 18 comment deadline has passed. The agencies issued the re-proposal on March 19, 2026 on a six-to-one Fed vote, with finalization expected in Q4 2026 and implementation beginning in 2027. For finance transformation consultants, this is the transition from "assessing the proposal" to "building the implementation program." The shift from internal models to the Standardized Approach transforms how operational risk teams organize their work, what data they collect, and how they report to the board -- and that reengineering requirement touches finance data infrastructure directly.
**Theme 2 (New): Deposit Mix Divergence as a Planning Variable**
Not all super-regionals are experiencing deposit cost normalization identically. At Bank of America, NII rose sequentially but missed consensus, and deposit mix is worsening: non-interest-bearing deposits fell while clients moved to CDs and money markets, pushing funding costs up and capping NIM expansion. Meanwhile, at Regions, consumer deposits continued to grow with checking balance increases, and total deposit costs fell to one point one eight percent. This bifurcation -- between franchise-funded regionals and capital-markets-dependent universals -- is a materially different CFO planning problem and changes assumptions in NII scenario modeling.
**Theme 3 (Evolving): AI Is Entering the Workforce Accounting Phase**
According to Bloomberg Intelligence, Wall Street banks are projected to cut up to two hundred thousand jobs over the next few years due to intelligent automation. Junior associates and entry-level analysts are among the most affected, as their roles often involve routine reporting and basic financial modeling. The most significant displacement occurs in positions dedicated to basic bookkeeping, transactional accounting, and manual data entry. The CFO agenda item has shifted from "are we piloting AI" to "how do we account for headcount reductions, manage remaining talent, and govern hybrid human-AI workflows."
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**KeyCorp Pre-Print (Reports July 21):** In Q1 2026, KeyCorp posted net income of four hundred eighty-six million dollars, or forty-four cents per diluted share, revenue of one point nine five billion dollars up ten percent year-over-year, and net interest margin of two point eight seven percent -- up five basis points sequentially. C&I loans account for roughly fifty percent of KeyCorp's average loan balances, and demand was robust in Q2. Tomorrow's print will determine whether the NIM recovery trajectory is intact heading into the Q3 rate decision.
**Regions Post-Print Detail:** Asset quality improved, with net charge-offs of one hundred two million dollars or zero point four two percent of average loans, down from zero point five four percent in Q1 2026. Regions management guided for NIM flat to slightly up in Q3, with key drivers including fixed asset turnover and a hedge rate increase, targeting approximately three point seven zero percent by year-end.
**Fifth Third Surprise:** Per the AlphaStreet ticker, Fifth Third Bancorp posted a forty-six percent revenue jump in Q2 2026, beating on EPS. That is a significantly higher revenue growth figure than peers and will reset analyst expectations for the combined Comerica book.
**Truist Beats:** Truist Financial delivered a twelve point eight percent Q2 2026 upside, with revenue up six percent -- clearing the wall of pre-print analyst downgrades flagged in prior episodes.
**BofA Deposit Mix Warning:** The universal bank read-across is not uniformly positive. Bank of America's quarter beat was driven by a seventy percent jump in equities trading and a fifty percent jump in investment banking -- both cyclical. NII missed consensus, and deposit mix worsened as clients moved to CDs and money markets.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame -- Post-Comment Phase (Evolving):** The June 18 comment close puts the rule in active agency review. The March 2026 re-proposal delivers net capital relief of about eighty-seven point seven billion dollars versus the original framework's nineteen percent capital increase, with finalization expected in late 2026 and implementation in 2027. Recalibration could create opportunities for banks to reassess binding constraints, release excess management buffers, and redeploy capital toward lending growth, balance sheet optimization, and M&A. The finance function implication: treasury teams must now model capital redeployment scenarios, not just compliance scenarios.
**Regional Bank Capital (New Angle):** Prior rule changes under the current administration around stress tests would bring cumulative capital reduction to four point eight percent for large banks, five point two percent for midsize banks, and seven point eight percent for smaller banks. Banks should also consider the recently adjusted CBLR framework, with the community bank leverage ratio threshold lowered to eight percent effective July 2026. Community bank controllers need to reassess whether CBLR opt-in remains optimal under the new threshold.
**Regulatory Fragmentation Across Jurisdictions:** This divergence between the US capital relief package and EU/UK requirements creates a period of regulatory fragmentation: European banks may face higher capital requirements than US competitors for equivalent risk exposures, affecting competitive dynamics in global capital markets, cross-border lending, and M&A advisory. For super-regionals with cross-border activity, this is a pricing advantage and a competitive intelligence item.
---
### AI in Finance
**The Workforce Accounting Reality:** AI can automate routine tasks and potentially impact entry-level finance and junior roles. This shift is also creating new, specialized "hybrid" roles that require human oversight, strategic interpretation, and ethical judgment, including AI automation engineers and AI governance and compliance managers. The CFO agenda item is no longer "will AI reduce headcount" but "how do we account for these structural shifts in workforce planning, compensation budgets, and FTE-to-output ratios."
**BCG Diagnosis on Where Banks Actually Are:** A Boston Consulting Group report notes that most banks are deploying AI for basic activities rather than those that drive transformation. To fix this, companies are looking for specialized human teams who can use AI tools to drive high-level business growth. This is the most important buying signal for transformation consultants: the "basic activity" saturation point has been reached, and clients are now ready to fund AI work that touches strategy, scenario modeling, and regulatory reporting.
**FP&A AI Adoption Gap:** Technavio projects the AI in FP&A market to grow by forty-eight point eight seven billion dollars by 2029. Yet the FP&A Trends Survey 2025 reveals that fifty-three percent of organizations still do not use AI in any FP&A process. That fifty-three percent is the addressable market for finance transformation work. Banks in that cohort face a compounding disadvantage as peers close planning cycles faster and run more scenarios.
**Buy-Side AI Literacy Signal:** A Traders Magazine and Aiera survey finds that seventy-seven percent of buy-side firms currently have organization-wide deployments of generative AI platforms in place. Seventy-seven percent said broker research was the most valuable input to receive as machine-readable feeds directly into their internal AI systems, followed by earnings transcripts at fifty-seven percent and market data at forty-two percent. The read-across for bank finance teams: the data consumption model is shifting to machine-readable ingestion, which has direct implications for how banks produce and publish regulatory and financial disclosures.
**Vendor Positioning:** The biggest finance technology trend in 2026 is AI moving from standalone features into the daily workflow of ERP, FP&A, payroll, AP, and spend management platforms. Vendors like Vena are introducing AI-enabled planning, querying, and analytics, allowing users to generate forecasts, scenarios, and insights with simple prompts, with results including faster planning cycles, improved accuracy, and a more self-sufficient FP&A function. For bank buyers, the evaluation question has shifted from "does the platform have AI" to "which workflows are natively AI-enabled versus bolted on."
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The Nine-Day Clock:** The July 29 FOMC meeting is nine days away. The June SEP turned notably more hawkish: the median projection for the federal funds rate at end-2026 rose to three point eight percent, and nine of eighteen participants penciled in at least one rate hike this year. Finance teams running annual NII plans must now stress-test a rate hike scenario alongside a hold -- the FOMC hold is the base case, but a twenty-five basis point increase cannot be dismissed, and the planning asymmetry has real NIM and funding cost implications.
**Capital Redeployment Planning:** With the Basel re-proposal delivering net relief, the package lowers capital requirements overall, reduces duplication, and improves the economics of traditional lending. It also creates new strategic and operational questions for treasury, risk, finance, reporting, and data teams as firms assess the impact and prepare for implementation. Treasury functions that have been holding excess buffers against the original nineteen percent increase must now rebuild their capital allocation models -- a genuine finance transformation trigger.
**IBM CFO Survey Benchmark:** According to IBM Institute for Business Value research, sixty-nine percent of CFOs say that AI is integral to their finance transformation strategy. At banks where that statement is aspirational rather than operational, the gap to peers is widening with each quarter.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The conventional wisdom after this earnings cycle is that super-regionals have successfully navigated deposit repricing. But the BofA data tells a more nuanced story: non-interest-bearing deposits fell while clients moved to CDs and money markets, pushing funding costs up and capping NIM expansion. For super-regionals with similarly elevated wealth and commercial client bases -- particularly those with growing private bank books -- the assumption that deposit beta improvement is durable may be premature. If rates stay higher for longer, the higher-balance clients who repriced into money markets in 2025 have no strong incentive to move back into demand deposits. CFOs should not model deposit cost normalization as a one-way journey; the mix may prove stickier than the headline cost number suggests.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The Basel clock is now running:** The June 18 comment close means the post-comment implementation planning phase has started. Ask your client: what is the sequencing of their data, systems, and reporting workstreams for a 2027 implementation date? Large banks should plan for a 12-to-18-month implementation window from final-rule issuance. That window opens the moment the final rule drops -- likely Q4 -- and finance infrastructure work that hasn't begun now will compress into an already crowded change calendar.
2. **The BCG AI diagnosis is a buying trigger:** Most banks are using AI for basic tasks. BCG notes that most banks are deploying AI for basic activities rather than those that drive transformation, and companies are now looking for specialized teams to drive high-level business growth with AI tools. The transition from basic to transformational AI in finance -- scenario modeling, regulatory reporting automation, close acceleration -- is where the next wave of finance technology spend is concentrating. Ask your client where their AI investments rank on that spectrum.
3. **Deposit mix is a CFO planning variable, not just a treasury metric:** The divergence between Regions' consumer deposit growth and BofA's NIB-to-CD migration is a structural story, not a rate story. For any super-regional with a meaningful wealth or commercial banking franchise, the CFO needs a deposit behavior model that goes beyond cost -- one that models mix stability under rate scenarios, because the "stickiness" assumption embedded in most NII models may be optimistic.
