I'll run parallel searches across all key coverage areas simultaneously to surface what's genuinely new for July 17, 2026 — the final day of Q2 super-regional earnings week, after Truist, Fifth Third, Regions, and Citizens have all reported.Now let me get one more targeted search to capture what's genuinely new today: Truist's actual Q2 results, Regions and Citizens prints, and the July 29 FOMC hike probability after the June CPI data.I now have comprehensive data to construct today's briefing. The genuinely new angles for July 17 are: (1) Citizens Financial's actual Q2 print is live -- a forty-one percent year-over-year EPS gain, NIM up ten basis points in the first half, and a private bank deposit surge from eight point seven billion to eighteen point three billion that is the most distinctive structural story of the super-regional cohort this week; (2) Truist reports this morning as the final print of the week, with CEO leadership transition to Michael Lyons as a concurrent governance angle that no prior episode touched; (3) the July twenty-nine FOMC meeting is now twelve days away with CME FedWatch at forty-six percent probability of a hike, making the post-earnings-week transition to pure rate-decision positioning the new CFO planning challenge; (4) the Basel III re-proposal comment period closed June eighteenth, placing the agenda firmly in post-comment finalization territory; (5) the Oliver Wyman / NYSE CFO Survey finding that banking CFOs are the most AI-aggressive sector -- eighty-eight percent planning moderate-to-substantial spending increases -- with controls, audit, and fraud detection as the top deployment area rather than FP&A, is an unexplored angle distinct from all prior recaps; and (6) the Gartner / Bain / BCG data convergence on the confidence gap: only thirty-six percent of CFOs feel assured they can drive AI enterprise impact, yet sixty percent are increasing finance AI budgets by ten percent or more this year.
---
## Finance Pulse | Friday, July 17, 2026
**Bottom line: The Q2 super-regional earnings season closes today with Citizens printing the most compelling structural story of the cohort -- a forty-one percent EPS surge powered by a private banking deposit engine that doubled in twelve months -- while Truist reports this morning against a leadership-transition backdrop; twelve days out from a near-coin-flip July 29 FOMC decision, the planning question for bank CFOs shifts from "what did Q2 deliver" to "what scenario do we run for Q3 if the Fed hikes in two weeks."**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. **Citizens Financial delivered the week's standout super-regional print**: Q2 net income of five hundred eighty-seven million dollars, EPS of one dollar thirty cents (up forty-one percent year over year), ROTCE of thirteen point nine percent, and NIM expansion of ten basis points across the first half of twenty-twenty-six -- with full-year NIM guided to three point twenty-two to three point twenty-seven percent. 2. **Truist reports today under dual pressure**: The street expects one dollar eight cents on five point two four billion in revenue, but the more consequential watch point is CFO Mike Maguire's NIM and deposit-cost disclosure alongside the CEO transition to incoming CEO Michael Lyons -- making this simultaneously an earnings event and an operating-model signal. 3. **The July 29 FOMC meeting is now a near-coin-flip**: CME FedWatch put a hike probability at forty-six point five percent as of July thirteenth, and Fed Governor Waller's warning not to "repeat the mistakes of twenty-twenty-one and twenty-twenty-two" has kept that probability elevated even as June CPI was expected to cool from four point two percent to three point eight percent year-over-year. 4. **Basel III re-proposal is post-comment**: The June eighteenth comment deadline has passed. The revised March twenty-sixth proposal -- which formally rescinds the twenty-twenty-three framework, removes the dual-stack approach, and is expected to modestly decrease overall capital -- now awaits finalization, with Bloomberg Intelligence estimating a final rule by Q4 twenty-twenty-six and implementation beginning as early as twenty-twenty-seven. 5. **Banking CFOs are the most AI-aggressive sector in finance**: The Oliver Wyman / NYSE CFO Survey found eighty-eight percent of banking and capital markets CFOs plan moderate or substantial enterprise AI spending increases, with controls, audit, and fraud detection -- not FP&A -- as the leading deployment area.
---
### Three Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The Private Banking Deposit Surge as a Finance-Function Structural Story**
Citizens' private bank is the week's most underreported super-regional development from a finance transformation standpoint. Spot deposits in the private bank reached eighteen point three billion dollars, up from eight point seven billion a year earlier, while average deposits grew to seventeen point eight billion. The private bank contributed fifteen cents to EPS, representing eleven point five percent of total pre-tax income, and maintained a return on equity exceeding twenty-five percent. For bank CFOs and finance transformation consultants, this is not just a revenue story: a private banking deposit base that doubles in twelve months changes the liability mix, the deposit-cost modeling, the funds-transfer-pricing architecture, and the FP&A scenario universe simultaneously. When the deposit engine grows at this velocity, the finance function must rebuild its NIM and margin models in near real time -- a direct forcing function for data platform and planning tool investment.
**Theme 2 (New): The Post-Comment Basel III Window -- What Comes Next for Capital and Reporting Infrastructure**
The U.S. banking agencies have proposed a new capital package that revisits Basel III Endgame for the largest firms, introduces a separate approach for regional and smaller banks, and revises the GSIB surcharge framework. Taken together, the package lowers capital requirements overall, reduces duplication across the framework, and improves the economics of traditional lending -- but it also creates new strategic and operational questions for treasury, risk, finance, reporting, and data teams as firms assess the impact and prepare for implementation. With comments now closed, the actionable CFO question is no longer "what do we comment on" but "what do we build." A primary change is the removal of the dual-stack framework where banks calculate capital ratios using both standardized and internal models; the updated proposal emphasizes a simpler structure to reduce complexity and improve transparency, with regulators signaling a clear preference for standardized methodologies, replacing bank-specific models with a "common language" that enhances comparability and provides long-term capital predictability. That shift from internal models to standardized approaches is a data and technology rebuild, not just a capital number -- precisely the kind of multi-year infrastructure investment that lands in the finance transformation budget.
**Theme 3 (Evolving): The AI Confidence Gap Widens as Bank CFOs Lead Sector Spending**
Banking and capital markets CFOs are the most aggressive on AI, with eighty-eight percent planning moderate or substantial enterprise spending increases; their leading investment area is controls, audit, and fraud detection -- a reflection of an industry where the cost of error is measured in regulatory consequence as much as financial loss. Yet the returns remain elusive. Gartner research found that just thirty-six percent of CFOs feel assured they can drive meaningful enterprise impact from AI, even as investment continues to climb -- a gap that arguably offers the clearest evidence that AI adoption in finance has outpaced the operating models, data foundations, and skills needed to make it pay off. The Bain twenty-twenty-six CFO Survey provides the clearest ROI signal to date: among all CFOs, thirty-one percent rate AI outcomes as strongly positive; among those who have scaled AI into full production, that figure rises to forty-one percent, compared with twenty-five percent among those still in pilot mode; among top-quartile organizations by AI maturity, it exceeds sixty percent -- meaning the return on AI investment is not primarily a function of how much you spend but of how far you scale.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**Citizens Financial (Q2 live print):** Diluted EPS of one dollar thirty cents represented a forty-one percent increase from the prior year period, while tangible book value per share grew to thirty-eight dollars twenty-nine cents, up nine percent year-over-year. Net interest income emerged as a primary growth driver, increasing four point four percent sequentially to one point six three one billion dollars; NIM on a fully taxable-equivalent basis expanded three basis points to three point one seven percent, benefiting from lower terminated swap impacts, non-core portfolio runoff, and fixed-rate asset repricing. Revenue is trending above initial guidance, which combined with expense discipline, puts Citizens on track to deliver over six hundred basis points of positive operating leverage for the full year, with a clear path to a sixteen to eighteen percent ROTCE target by the end of twenty-twenty-seven.
**Truist (Q1 twenty-twenty-six baseline into today's print):** Net income available to common shareholders was one point four billion dollars in Q1 twenty-twenty-six, up nineteen percent year-over-year; total taxable-equivalent revenue rose five point one percent; net interest income increased eighty-nine million dollars or two point five percent, driven by fixed-rate asset repricing and loan growth; and NIM on a taxable-equivalent basis was three point zero two percent, up one basis point from Q1 twenty-twenty-five. Truist carries the weakest year-to-date stock performance in the super-regional cohort -- a gain of only five percent -- into today's print, making any upside surprise in NIM or deposit cost particularly market-moving.
**Rate and funding context:** Under the most likely economic outlook, many Fed officials expected rates to end the year at or slightly below the current level; the Fed kept the federal funds rate unchanged at three point fifty to three point seventy-five percent in June, in line with expectations. But the dot plot indicated a median funds rate projection of three point eight percent by year-end -- suggesting a hike is very much on the table. Core PCE inflation rose from three point zero percent in December twenty-twenty-five to three point three percent in April twenty-twenty-six, giving policymakers less confidence that inflation is moving steadily toward target.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame -- post-comment phase:** After nearly three years of controversy, the U.S. Basel III Endgame is getting a do-over; on March nineteenth, twenty-twenty-six, the Fed, OCC, and FDIC issued three proposals that would comprehensively overhaul the existing U.S. bank capital framework. The agencies anticipate that the amount of overall capital in the banking system "would modestly decrease" if the proposals are implemented, although they expect levels would remain "substantially higher" than pre-financial-crisis levels. For super-regionals, the critical new feature is a separate, less burdensome approach for firms outside the Category I / II tier -- meaning the bifurcation of capital reporting logic between universals and regionals is now the implementation design question. Bloomberg Intelligence puts finalization as early as Q4 twenty-twenty-six, with implementation beginning as soon as twenty-twenty-seven.
**FOMC July 29 -- twelve-day countdown:** CME FedWatch estimates a forty-six point five percent probability of a twenty-five basis point hike; on Kalshi, the chances are thirty-six percent. The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for July twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and there is no Summary of Economic Projections produced for that meeting -- meaning bank CFOs and treasurers will have no dot-plot update to anchor forward NIM scenarios immediately after the decision.
---
### AI in Finance
The Oliver Wyman / NYSE CFO Survey twenty-twenty-six provides the sharpest sector-specific data point of the week: banking CFOs' leading AI investment area is controls, audit, and fraud detection; most AI deployment remains at pilot stage, with highest scaled deployment in order-to-cash; growth-oriented CFOs are about twice as likely as value-oriented peers to report AI at scale across key functions -- ten percent versus five percent -- and twenty-two percent of AI deployment leaders plan substantial enterprise spending increases in twenty-twenty-six, compared with fifteen percent of laggards.
On the buy-versus-build question: Deloitte research found that fifty-four percent of CFOs say integrating AI agents into finance is a top transformation priority for twenty-twenty-six, and nearly half of finance leaders who play a leading strategic role say they have already deployed specific AI agents; CFOs remain deliberately cautious about ceding full decision-making authority to autonomous systems in areas tied to financial controls and compliance, with near-term agents operating inside clearly defined, human-approved workflows.
The Deloitte CFO Technology Guide twenty-twenty-six raises the sharpest agentic AI governance question: as agents are deployed in different ways, CFOs may need a reality check -- as costs change, what will be the most useful and cost-efficient deployments, and in some cases, human labor may be more cost-effective than agents. That is a materially different frame from the vendor pitch, and it is the question that should anchor every AI-in-finance business case at a bank right now.
**Budget signals:** Gartner's twenty-twenty-six research found that three-quarters of CFOs are raising their technology budgets, with nearly half increasing spend by ten percent or more, as AI reshapes core finance, process automation, and analytics. A Bain survey of senior finance executives shows fifty-six percent are increasing enterprise-wide AI investment by more than fifteen percent this year; over the next two years, eighty-three percent of CFOs plan AI budget increases above fifteen percent, with forty-two percent expecting increases above thirty percent.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
The most actionable framing this week: finance transformation remains the top priority for CFOs for the third consecutive year, according to Gartner's Evanta community; this is not a one-off project but a continuous agenda item, driven by the need to do more with tighter resources in a volatile environment; AI and automation have surged to the second spot, reflecting a shift from exploration to execution.
The tension is structural: Gartner's twenty-twenty-six CFO Agenda research found that fifty-six percent rank enterprise-wide cost optimization among their top five priorities, while forty-seven percent simultaneously rank allocating capital to new growth opportunities in their top five -- a tension described as "very explicit" and showing up "every day" in conversations with finance chiefs.
In the most recent finance leader survey, fifty-one percent of CFOs cited talent retention and skills shortages as one of the top three barriers to delivering on finance strategy, even as fifty-eight percent said they were investing in AI and advanced analytics -- meaning CFOs are modernizing the function with a workforce that, by their own admission, doesn't yet have all the skills the modernization requires.
The Bain sequencing insight remains the clearest transformation guide: the organizations extracting real value from AI in finance are not those with the most advanced models -- they are the ones that made their processes consistent enough for those models to be useful.
---
### Contrarian Insight
**The Basel easing is not a planning win -- it is a planning rebuild.** Every coverage note this week frames the March twenty-twenty-six Basel re-proposal as capital relief. That is correct at the CET1 ratio level. But the shift from dual-stack to a single standardized approach, combined with the introduction of a separate regional bank tier, means banks must redesign their capital calculation infrastructure regardless of whether total capital goes up or down. The operational cost of rebuilding RWA data flows, reporting logic, and treasury scenario models to fit a fundamentally different framework is likely to exceed the economic value of the capital freed. Bank finance leaders should be budgeting for a multi-year capital reporting transformation program starting now -- not waiting for the final rule.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **"Citizens' private bank deposits doubled in twelve months -- is your deposit-mix model built to handle that velocity?"** When a single business line's deposit base grows from eight point seven to eighteen point three billion in a year, the FTP model, NIM forecast, and scenario architecture all break. Ask the client whether their planning infrastructure can reprice deposit segments in real time or whether it still runs on quarterly refresh cycles.
2. **"Your AI budget is going up thirty percent -- but only thirty-one percent of CFOs rate outcomes as strongly positive. What is your client's scale plan, not their pilot plan?"** The Bain data is unambiguous: satisfaction among scaled adopters is forty-one percent versus twenty-five percent for those still piloting. The conversation should be about sequencing (data foundation first, automation second, intelligence third) and the governance model that moves pilots into production, not the next demo.
3. **"The July twenty-ninth FOMC meeting produces no dot plot. How is your client modeling three NIM scenarios -- hold, hike, and hold-with-hawkish-guidance -- without a forward anchor?"** With no SEP at the July meeting, banks lose the single most useful external scenario anchor for H2 NIM planning. That gap is a direct forcing function for investing in scenario modeling capability inside the finance function.

## Finance Pulse | Friday, July 17, 2026

---
### Top Takeaways
1. **Citizens Financial delivered the week's standout super-regional print**: Q2 net income of five hundred eighty-seven million dollars, EPS of one dollar thirty cents (up forty-one percent year over year), ROTCE of thirteen point nine percent, and NIM expansion of ten basis points across the first half of twenty-twenty-six -- with full-year NIM guided to three point twenty-two to three point twenty-seven percent. 2. **Truist reports today under dual pressure**: The street expects one dollar eight cents on five point two four billion in revenue, but the more consequential watch point is CFO Mike Maguire's NIM and deposit-cost disclosure alongside the CEO transition to incoming CEO Michael Lyons -- making this simultaneously an earnings event and an operating-model signal. 3. **The July 29 FOMC meeting is now a near-coin-flip**: CME FedWatch put a hike probability at forty-six point five percent as of July thirteenth, and Fed Governor Waller's warning not to "repeat the mistakes of twenty-twenty-one and twenty-twenty-two" has kept that probability elevated even as June CPI was expected to cool from four point two percent to three point eight percent year-over-year. 4. **Basel III re-proposal is post-comment**: The June eighteenth comment deadline has passed. The revised March twenty-sixth proposal -- which formally rescinds the twenty-twenty-three framework, removes the dual-stack approach, and is expected to modestly decrease overall capital -- now awaits finalization, with Bloomberg Intelligence estimating a final rule by Q4 twenty-twenty-six and implementation beginning as early as twenty-twenty-seven. 5. **Banking CFOs are the most AI-aggressive sector in finance**: The Oliver Wyman / NYSE CFO Survey found eighty-eight percent of banking and capital markets CFOs plan moderate or substantial enterprise AI spending increases, with controls, audit, and fraud detection -- not FP&A -- as the leading deployment area.

**Theme 1 (New): The Private Banking Deposit Surge as a Finance-Function Structural Story**
Citizens' private bank is the week's most underreported super-regional development from a finance transformation standpoint. Spot deposits in the private bank reached eighteen point three billion dollars, up from eight point seven billion a year earlier, while average deposits grew to seventeen point eight billion. The private bank contributed fifteen cents to EPS, representing eleven point five percent of total pre-tax income, and maintained a return on equity exceeding twenty-five percent. For bank CFOs and finance transformation consultants, this is not just a revenue story: a private banking deposit base that doubles in twelve months changes the liability mix, the deposit-cost modeling, the funds-transfer-pricing architecture, and the FP&A scenario universe simultaneously. The U.S. banking agencies have proposed a new capital package that revisits Basel III Endgame for the largest firms, introduces a separate approach for regional and smaller banks, and revises the GSIB surcharge framework. ---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**Citizens Financial (Q2 live print):** Diluted EPS of one dollar thirty cents represented a forty-one percent increase from the prior year period, while tangible book value per share grew to thirty-eight dollars twenty-nine cents, up nine percent year-over-year. Net interest income emerged as a primary growth driver, increasing four point four percent sequentially to one point six three one billion dollars; NIM on a fully taxable-equivalent basis expanded three basis points to three point one seven percent, benefiting from lower terminated swap impacts, non-core portfolio runoff, and fixed-rate asset repricing. Revenue is trending above initial guidance, which combined with expense discipline, puts Citizens on track to deliver over six hundred basis points of positive operating leverage for the full year, with a clear path to a sixteen to eighteen percent ROTCE target by the end of twenty-twenty-seven.
**Truist (Q1 twenty-twenty-six baseline into today's print):** Net income available to common shareholders was one point four billion dollars in Q1 twenty-twenty-six, up nineteen percent year-over-year; total taxable-equivalent revenue rose five point one percent; net interest income increased eighty-nine million dollars or two point five percent, driven by fixed-rate asset repricing and loan growth; and NIM on a taxable-equivalent basis was three point zero two percent, up one basis point from Q1 twenty-twenty-five. Truist carries the weakest year-to-date stock performance in the super-regional cohort -- a gain of only five percent -- into today's print, making any upside surprise in NIM or deposit cost particularly market-moving.
**Rate and funding context:** Under the most likely economic outlook, many Fed officials expected rates to end the year at or slightly below the current level; the Fed kept the federal funds rate unchanged at three point fifty to three point seventy-five percent in June, in line with expectations. But the dot plot indicated a median funds rate projection of three point eight percent by year-end -- suggesting a hike is very much on the table. Core PCE inflation rose from three point zero percent in December twenty-twenty-five to three point three percent in April twenty-twenty-six, giving policymakers less confidence that inflation is moving steadily toward target.
---

**Basel III Endgame -- post-comment phase:** After nearly three years of controversy, the U.S. Basel III Endgame is getting a do-over; on March nineteenth, twenty-twenty-six, the Fed, OCC, and FDIC issued three proposals that would comprehensively overhaul the existing U.S. bank capital framework. The agencies anticipate that the amount of overall capital in the banking system "would modestly decrease" if the proposals are implemented, although they expect levels would remain "substantially higher" than pre-financial-crisis levels. The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for July twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and there is no Summary of Economic Projections produced for that meeting -- meaning bank CFOs and treasurers will have no dot-plot update to anchor forward NIM scenarios immediately after the decision.

item.title: Finance Pulse - Jul 16, 2026
item.description:
I'll run parallel searches across all key coverage areas simultaneously to surface what's genuinely new for July 16, 2026 — the day after PNC, M&T, and Morgan Stanley reported, and as the broader super-regional cohort prints.Now let me use my final search on U.S. Bancorp Q2 2026 results, which report today, and any PNC-specific results I haven't yet captured.I now have sufficient data across all coverage areas to produce today's briefing. The genuinely new angles for July 16 are: (1) U.S. Bancorp reports this morning (live earnings day for the super-regional cohort's most important payments/efficiency proxy); (2) M&T posted its highest-ever quarterly EPS and the credit quality improvement arc is now nine consecutive quarters, making it a distinct structural story; (3) Truist faces a wall of analyst downgrades pre-print ahead of tomorrow, while Fifth Third's first post-Comerica quarter is Friday, creating an M&A integration read-through angle not yet covered; (4) the Basel III post-comment-period dynamic has sharpened specifically around the Internal Loss Multiplier removal and its implications for operational risk capital; (5) the AI deployment sequencing debate has crystallized into a measurable "copilot-to-agent" production gap with specific ROI timelines; (6) the Warsh-era Fed communication shift away from forward guidance creates a new CFO planning challenge distinct from the rate-level debate covered previously.
---
## Finance Pulse | Thursday, July 16, 2026
**Bottom line: The super-regional earnings window is now live and producing a consistent read-across signal: credit quality has continued to improve, NII is tracking guidance, but deposit beta is a persistent open variable and expense pressure is intensifying just as Basel's Internal Loss Multiplier removal forces banks to rerun their entire operational risk capital stack from scratch.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. M&T Bank posted its highest quarterly diluted EPS in company history in Q2 2026, with credit metrics strengthening as criticized loans fell for the ninth consecutive quarter and net charge-offs dropping to twenty-three basis points. The nine-quarter credit improvement arc is now long enough to be structural, not cyclical.
2. U.S. Bancorp is releasing Q2 2026 results this morning before market open, with CEO Gunjan Kedia and CFO John Stern hosting the call at seven a.m. Central Time. Management had guided NII on a fully taxable equivalent basis to rise six to seven percent year over year, with the consensus estimate pegged at four point three four billion dollars, indicating a seven percent increase from the year-ago figure. USB is the cohort's most watched efficiency-ratio benchmark.
3. Fed Governor Christopher Waller's recent remarks have intensified speculation about a potential rate hike at the July twenty-eighth to twenty-ninth meeting, with the CME FedWatch tool assigning approximately twenty-five percent probability to a twenty-five basis point hike in July.
4. The single most consequential structural change in the March 2026 Basel III re-proposal is the removal of the Internal Loss Multiplier as a loss-history adjustment, meaning regulators will no longer adjust a firm's operational risk charge based on its loss record, effectively setting the ILM at one-point-zero for all U.S. banks.
5. CFO AI budgets are shifting from pilot experimentation toward structured deployment, with vendor evaluation now emphasizing ERP integration depth and data connector capabilities; CFOs who completed the shift from copilots to agentic AI platforms early are now in year two of production deployment, while pilot-focused organizations face widening competitive gaps.
---
### Three Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The M&T credit arc and its NIM compression signal** M&T guided full-year NII to the lower half of its seven-point-two to seven-point-three-five billion dollar range, with full-year NIM in the high three-sixty range. Management guided to some NIM compression in the second half relative to the approximately three-point-seven percent posted in the first half, driven by deposit pricing and loan yield dynamics. The cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta is guided to the low-to-mid-fifty percent range, which CFOs should treat as a sector floor assumption for second-half planning. This is the first time a super-regional CFO has explicitly quantified H2 NIM compression in this earnings cycle.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): Truist's multiple analyst downgrades and the operational credibility gap** Ahead of Truist's July 17 print, Bank of America Securities downgraded from Buy to Neutral, UBS downgraded from Buy to Neutral cutting the target from fifty-eight to fifty-five dollars, and Morgan Stanley slashed its target from sixty-two to fifty-four dollars while moving to Equal-Weight. Truist is the worst-performing name in the super-regional cohort with only a five percent year-to-date gain. For transformation consultants, this is the clearest live case of the market pricing operational execution risk into a post-merger integration story.
**Theme 3 (New): Basel operational risk ILM removal forces a full capital model rebuild** The ILM removal flips the preparation playbook entirely: programs that spent twelve months curating ten-year loss data for ILM inputs face a write-off of that effort, and RWA forecasts built against the 2023 NPR need rerunning against the 2026 numbers before the June eighteenth comment deadline, shifting the board conversation from raising capital to reshaping business mix. This creates immediate demand for capital calculation infrastructure, data re-architecture, and model governance modernization at every bank above one hundred billion dollars in assets.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**NIM and NII:** M&T's tax-equivalent NII rose four-point-eight percent year over year to one-point-eight-zero billion dollars, reflecting growth in average loans and investment securities along with favorable repricing of earning assets. Total loans reached one hundred forty-three-point-two billion dollars, up two-point-three percent from the prior quarter, while total deposits increased three-point-one percent sequentially to one hundred sixty-eight-point-nine billion dollars.
**Credit:** Net charge-offs decreased twenty-five-point-nine percent to eighty million dollars from the prior-year quarter, the provision for credit losses was one hundred twenty million dollars down four percent year over year, and non-performing assets declined twenty-three-point-two percent year over year to one-point-two-three billion dollars.
**Capital:** M&T Bank's estimated CET1 ratio was ten-point-one-nine percent, down from ten-point-nine-nine percent as of Q2 2025.
**Expenses:** M&T guided expenses to the high end of the five-point-five to five-point-six billion dollar range as the bank continues enterprise investments while maintaining expense discipline. This is the efficiency paradox in one sentence: banks are simultaneously cutting costs and investing, with the net being that the efficiency ratio is not improving as fast as the income line.
**Fee income:** M&T's fee income is expected at two-point-eight to two-point-eight-five billion dollars, reflecting year-to-date strength, the Bayview distribution, and higher sub-servicing fee income beginning in Q3.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame post-comment period:** The June eighteenth comment deadline has now passed. The March 2026 proposals revisit Basel III Endgame for the largest firms, introduce a separate approach for regional and smaller banks, revise the GSIB surcharge framework, lower capital requirements overall, reduce duplication, and improve economics of traditional lending, while creating new strategic and operational questions for treasury, risk, finance, reporting, and data teams.
The critical new operational angle: regulators project aggregate capital in the banking system will modestly decrease under the new framework, a dramatic pivot from the original plus-sixteen-percent CET1 increase, and the core objective is to replace internal models with standardized approaches that produce comparable, transparent requirements across institutions. For finance functions, standardized approaches mean the competitive edge shifts from model sophistication to data quality and reporting infrastructure.
The changes could materially affect bank capital requirements, profitability, product and service offerings, and long-term growth strategies; overall bank capital requirements are expected to decrease due to lower minimum risk weights and less conservative methodologies, though the 2026 capital rules also add complexity and will require careful implementation.
---
### AI in Finance
**What is genuinely deployed vs. marketed:** The headline shift of 2026 is from experimentation to governed deployment; banks started asking how to supervise AI agents, and according to a Wolters Kluwer survey, forty-four percent of finance teams expected to use agentic AI in 2026, a steep increase over the prior year.
**What is working and where:** Compliance and financial crime emerged as the leading use case, with real-time monitoring replacing periodic review in early deployments; among agentic AI use cases, regulatory-change triage, financial-crime detection, and controls monitoring drew the most attention because each pairs high volume with a containable cost of error.
**The governance gap that creates transformation work:** The gap between piloting and impact stems from architectural limitations: most finance teams are adding AI inside existing functional lanes, with AP getting invoice automation, FP&A getting forecasting tools, and close teams getting reconciliation support, but each system carries its own data model, workflow logic, and audit trail, and disconnection shows up at the seams where approved spend becomes an invoice, an invoice becomes a journal entry, and a journal entry becomes a forecast assumption.
**Sequencing and ROI timelines:** Across organizations deploying autonomous finance in production, AP automation typically deploys first due to high volume and measurable baseline metrics, reconciliation and close automation follows, FP&A forecast refresh automates once operational data quality improves, and AR collections automates last due to external data dependencies; each phase builds data quality and governance infrastructure that the next phase depends on.
**CFO budget signal:** Deloitte's Q4 2025 CFO Signals survey found that fifty-four percent of CFOs say integrating AI agents into their finance departments will be a top transformation priority in 2026, and eighty-seven percent believe AI will be extremely or very important to finance operations this year.
**The Gartner warning CFOs must own:** Gartner predicts that over forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027. That number is the single most important governance mandate for any bank CFO approving agentic AI spend right now.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The new planning uncertainty is not about rate level, it is about Fed communication style.** The rate has been held steady for four consecutive FOMC meetings, the most recent on June seventeenth, under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's leadership. Chair Warsh's first meeting signaled less forward guidance and a broader review of Fed communications, balance sheet policy, and inflation framework. CFOs who built planning models around Powell-era guidance granularity must now operate with a structurally less transparent signal. That is a direct FP&A infrastructure challenge, not just a macro one.
**The deposit beta number that changes planning assumptions:** M&T's explicit call of cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta in the low-to-mid-fifty percent range is the first publicly quantified anchor from the super-regional cohort this cycle. CFOs at peer institutions should stress-test whether their own deposit cost assumptions are consistent with or divergent from this figure.
**Agentic AI sequencing as a buying signal:** Task-specific agents for invoice processing and reconciliation typically pay back in four to nine months; a single workflow such as AP or close reaches full value in four to six months; a portfolio of agents across the CFO office reaches full value in twelve to eighteen months; and timeline is driven by data readiness and change management, not the underlying AI technology. For bank finance transformation leaders, this is the ROI framing that wins budget approval.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus narrative is that lower Basel III capital requirements are unambiguously good for banks. But the operational cost of compliance with the 2026 re-proposal may be higher, not lower, than the 2023 framework for many super-regionals. The combined 2026 proposals exceed fifteen hundred pages and address nearly every section of the existing regulatory capital requirements. The shift from internal models to standardized approaches does not reduce reporting work; it changes the source of the number while demanding new data pipelines to feed standardized formulas. Banks that invested in sophisticated internal models are not relieved of cost; they are redirecting investment from model maintenance to data infrastructure and regulatory reporting uplift. The finance function workload goes up even as nominal capital requirements come down.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **M&T's deposit beta anchor vs. your client's assumptions:** M&T has explicitly guided cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta to the low-to-mid-fifty percent range for the full year. Where does your client's deposit cost model sit relative to that, and what does the delta imply for their second-half NII forecast?
2. **The ILM removal write-off problem:** Banks that spent the last twelve months building ten-year loss data programs for Internal Loss Multiplier inputs in the 2023 Basel framework now need to redirect that investment toward standardized approach data infrastructure. Is your client's capital data architecture team aware that the work product has changed, not just the capital outcome?
3. **The Gartner cancellation rate and governance readiness:** With Gartner projecting that more than forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by 2027, what is your client's governance framework for distinguishing projects that survive from those that do not, and is there a CFO-owned kill criteria built into the approval process?

I'll run parallel searches across all key coverage areas simultaneously to surface what's genuinely new for July 16, 2026 — the day after PNC, M&T, and Morgan Stanley reported, and as the broader super-regional cohort prints.Now let me use my final search on U.S. Bancorp Q2 2026 results, which report today, and any PNC-specific results I haven't yet captured.I now have sufficient data across all coverage areas to produce today's briefing. The genuinely new angles for July 16 are: (1) U.S. Bancorp reports this morning (live earnings day for the super-regional cohort's most important payments/efficiency proxy); (2) M&T posted its highest-ever quarterly EPS and the credit quality improvement arc is now nine consecutive quarters, making it a distinct structural story; (3) Truist faces a wall of analyst downgrades pre-print ahead of tomorrow, while Fifth Third's first post-Comerica quarter is Friday, creating an M&A integration read-through angle not yet covered; (4) the Basel III post-comment-period dynamic has sharpened specifically around the Internal Loss Multiplier removal and its implications for operational risk capital; (5) the AI deployment sequencing debate has crystallized into a measurable "copilot-to-agent" production gap with specific ROI timelines; (6) the Warsh-era Fed communication shift away from forward guidance creates a new CFO planning challenge distinct from the rate-level debate covered previously.
---
## Finance Pulse | Thursday, July 16, 2026
**Bottom line: The super-regional earnings window is now live and producing a consistent read-across signal: credit quality has continued to improve, NII is tracking guidance, but deposit beta is a persistent open variable and expense pressure is intensifying just as Basel's Internal Loss Multiplier removal forces banks to rerun their entire operational risk capital stack from scratch.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. M&T Bank posted its highest quarterly diluted EPS in company history in Q2 2026, with credit metrics strengthening as criticized loans fell for the ninth consecutive quarter and net charge-offs dropping to twenty-three basis points. The nine-quarter credit improvement arc is now long enough to be structural, not cyclical.
2. U.S. Bancorp is releasing Q2 2026 results this morning before market open, with CEO Gunjan Kedia and CFO John Stern hosting the call at seven a.m. Central Time. Management had guided NII on a fully taxable equivalent basis to rise six to seven percent year over year, with the consensus estimate pegged at four point three four billion dollars, indicating a seven percent increase from the year-ago figure. USB is the cohort's most watched efficiency-ratio benchmark.
3. Fed Governor Christopher Waller's recent remarks have intensified speculation about a potential rate hike at the July twenty-eighth to twenty-ninth meeting, with the CME FedWatch tool assigning approximately twenty-five percent probability to a twenty-five basis point hike in July.
4. The single most consequential structural change in the March 2026 Basel III re-proposal is the removal of the Internal Loss Multiplier as a loss-history adjustment, meaning regulators will no longer adjust a firm's operational risk charge based on its loss record, effectively setting the ILM at one-point-zero for all U.S. banks.
5. CFO AI budgets are shifting from pilot experimentation toward structured deployment, with vendor evaluation now emphasizing ERP integration depth and data connector capabilities; CFOs who completed the shift from copilots to agentic AI platforms early are now in year two of production deployment, while pilot-focused organizations face widening competitive gaps.
---
### Three Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The M&T credit arc and its NIM compression signal** M&T guided full-year NII to the lower half of its seven-point-two to seven-point-three-five billion dollar range, with full-year NIM in the high three-sixty range. Management guided to some NIM compression in the second half relative to the approximately three-point-seven percent posted in the first half, driven by deposit pricing and loan yield dynamics. The cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta is guided to the low-to-mid-fifty percent range, which CFOs should treat as a sector floor assumption for second-half planning. This is the first time a super-regional CFO has explicitly quantified H2 NIM compression in this earnings cycle.
**Theme 2 (Evolving): Truist's multiple analyst downgrades and the operational credibility gap** Ahead of Truist's July 17 print, Bank of America Securities downgraded from Buy to Neutral, UBS downgraded from Buy to Neutral cutting the target from fifty-eight to fifty-five dollars, and Morgan Stanley slashed its target from sixty-two to fifty-four dollars while moving to Equal-Weight. Truist is the worst-performing name in the super-regional cohort with only a five percent year-to-date gain. For transformation consultants, this is the clearest live case of the market pricing operational execution risk into a post-merger integration story.
**Theme 3 (New): Basel operational risk ILM removal forces a full capital model rebuild** The ILM removal flips the preparation playbook entirely: programs that spent twelve months curating ten-year loss data for ILM inputs face a write-off of that effort, and RWA forecasts built against the 2023 NPR need rerunning against the 2026 numbers before the June eighteenth comment deadline, shifting the board conversation from raising capital to reshaping business mix. This creates immediate demand for capital calculation infrastructure, data re-architecture, and model governance modernization at every bank above one hundred billion dollars in assets.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**NIM and NII:** M&T's tax-equivalent NII rose four-point-eight percent year over year to one-point-eight-zero billion dollars, reflecting growth in average loans and investment securities along with favorable repricing of earning assets. Total loans reached one hundred forty-three-point-two billion dollars, up two-point-three percent from the prior quarter, while total deposits increased three-point-one percent sequentially to one hundred sixty-eight-point-nine billion dollars.
**Credit:** Net charge-offs decreased twenty-five-point-nine percent to eighty million dollars from the prior-year quarter, the provision for credit losses was one hundred twenty million dollars down four percent year over year, and non-performing assets declined twenty-three-point-two percent year over year to one-point-two-three billion dollars.
**Capital:** M&T Bank's estimated CET1 ratio was ten-point-one-nine percent, down from ten-point-nine-nine percent as of Q2 2025.
**Expenses:** M&T guided expenses to the high end of the five-point-five to five-point-six billion dollar range as the bank continues enterprise investments while maintaining expense discipline. This is the efficiency paradox in one sentence: banks are simultaneously cutting costs and investing, with the net being that the efficiency ratio is not improving as fast as the income line.
**Fee income:** M&T's fee income is expected at two-point-eight to two-point-eight-five billion dollars, reflecting year-to-date strength, the Bayview distribution, and higher sub-servicing fee income beginning in Q3.
---
### Regulatory Radar
**Basel III Endgame post-comment period:** The June eighteenth comment deadline has now passed. The March 2026 proposals revisit Basel III Endgame for the largest firms, introduce a separate approach for regional and smaller banks, revise the GSIB surcharge framework, lower capital requirements overall, reduce duplication, and improve economics of traditional lending, while creating new strategic and operational questions for treasury, risk, finance, reporting, and data teams.
The critical new operational angle: regulators project aggregate capital in the banking system will modestly decrease under the new framework, a dramatic pivot from the original plus-sixteen-percent CET1 increase, and the core objective is to replace internal models with standardized approaches that produce comparable, transparent requirements across institutions. For finance functions, standardized approaches mean the competitive edge shifts from model sophistication to data quality and reporting infrastructure.
The changes could materially affect bank capital requirements, profitability, product and service offerings, and long-term growth strategies; overall bank capital requirements are expected to decrease due to lower minimum risk weights and less conservative methodologies, though the 2026 capital rules also add complexity and will require careful implementation.
---
### AI in Finance
**What is genuinely deployed vs. marketed:** The headline shift of 2026 is from experimentation to governed deployment; banks started asking how to supervise AI agents, and according to a Wolters Kluwer survey, forty-four percent of finance teams expected to use agentic AI in 2026, a steep increase over the prior year.
**What is working and where:** Compliance and financial crime emerged as the leading use case, with real-time monitoring replacing periodic review in early deployments; among agentic AI use cases, regulatory-change triage, financial-crime detection, and controls monitoring drew the most attention because each pairs high volume with a containable cost of error.
**The governance gap that creates transformation work:** The gap between piloting and impact stems from architectural limitations: most finance teams are adding AI inside existing functional lanes, with AP getting invoice automation, FP&A getting forecasting tools, and close teams getting reconciliation support, but each system carries its own data model, workflow logic, and audit trail, and disconnection shows up at the seams where approved spend becomes an invoice, an invoice becomes a journal entry, and a journal entry becomes a forecast assumption.
**Sequencing and ROI timelines:** Across organizations deploying autonomous finance in production, AP automation typically deploys first due to high volume and measurable baseline metrics, reconciliation and close automation follows, FP&A forecast refresh automates once operational data quality improves, and AR collections automates last due to external data dependencies; each phase builds data quality and governance infrastructure that the next phase depends on.
**CFO budget signal:** Deloitte's Q4 2025 CFO Signals survey found that fifty-four percent of CFOs say integrating AI agents into their finance departments will be a top transformation priority in 2026, and eighty-seven percent believe AI will be extremely or very important to finance operations this year.
**The Gartner warning CFOs must own:** Gartner predicts that over forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027. That number is the single most important governance mandate for any bank CFO approving agentic AI spend right now.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The new planning uncertainty is not about rate level, it is about Fed communication style.** The rate has been held steady for four consecutive FOMC meetings, the most recent on June seventeenth, under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's leadership. Chair Warsh's first meeting signaled less forward guidance and a broader review of Fed communications, balance sheet policy, and inflation framework. CFOs who built planning models around Powell-era guidance granularity must now operate with a structurally less transparent signal. That is a direct FP&A infrastructure challenge, not just a macro one.
**The deposit beta number that changes planning assumptions:** M&T's explicit call of cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta in the low-to-mid-fifty percent range is the first publicly quantified anchor from the super-regional cohort this cycle. CFOs at peer institutions should stress-test whether their own deposit cost assumptions are consistent with or divergent from this figure.
**Agentic AI sequencing as a buying signal:** Task-specific agents for invoice processing and reconciliation typically pay back in four to nine months; a single workflow such as AP or close reaches full value in four to six months; a portfolio of agents across the CFO office reaches full value in twelve to eighteen months; and timeline is driven by data readiness and change management, not the underlying AI technology. For bank finance transformation leaders, this is the ROI framing that wins budget approval.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus narrative is that lower Basel III capital requirements are unambiguously good for banks. But the operational cost of compliance with the 2026 re-proposal may be higher, not lower, than the 2023 framework for many super-regionals. The combined 2026 proposals exceed fifteen hundred pages and address nearly every section of the existing regulatory capital requirements. The shift from internal models to standardized approaches does not reduce reporting work; it changes the source of the number while demanding new data pipelines to feed standardized formulas. Banks that invested in sophisticated internal models are not relieved of cost; they are redirecting investment from model maintenance to data infrastructure and regulatory reporting uplift. The finance function workload goes up even as nominal capital requirements come down.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **M&T's deposit beta anchor vs. your client's assumptions:** M&T has explicitly guided cumulative interest-bearing deposit beta to the low-to-mid-fifty percent range for the full year. Where does your client's deposit cost model sit relative to that, and what does the delta imply for their second-half NII forecast?
2. **The ILM removal write-off problem:** Banks that spent the last twelve months building ten-year loss data programs for Internal Loss Multiplier inputs in the 2023 Basel framework now need to redirect that investment toward standardized approach data infrastructure. Is your client's capital data architecture team aware that the work product has changed, not just the capital outcome?
3. **The Gartner cancellation rate and governance readiness:** With Gartner projecting that more than forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by 2027, what is your client's governance framework for distinguishing projects that survive from those that do not, and is there a CFO-owned kill criteria built into the approval process?

item.title: Finance Pulse - Jul 15, 2026
item.description:
I'll run parallel searches across all key coverage areas to surface what's genuinely new for July 15, 2026 -- the morning after the first wave of Q2 earnings prints.Good. Now I have the earnings calendar and macro picture. Let me search for the two most critical remaining areas: the actual Q2 earnings results that came out this morning (PNC, M&T, Morgan Stanley) and the AI-in-finance / regulatory angles.I now have strong data across all coverage areas. Let me synthesize everything into today's briefing. The genuinely new angles for July 15 are: (1) the super-regional earnings window has arrived -- PNC and M&T report this morning, Citizens tomorrow, Regions/Truist/Fifth Third Friday; (2) Fifth Third's Comerica acquisition ($10.9B) is a fresh and unexamined M&A integration angle; (3) Morgan Stanley reports Q2 today, providing the wealth management / fee income read-across; (4) Fed Chair Warsh's Congressional testimony this week (Semiannual Monetary Policy Report) with his "price stability mentioned twelve times" framing; (5) the G-SIB surcharge trajectory (5.2% by 2028, up from 4.5%) creating a $20B capital rebuild story; (6) the Gartner prediction that 40%+ of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end of 2027; and (7) the BCG/Bain convergence on AI sequencing failure mode -- data foundation before automation before intelligence -- as the CFO buying pattern signal. Let me now construct both outputs.
---
## Finance Pulse | Wednesday, July 15, 2026
**Bottom line: The super-regional earnings window opens this morning -- PNC and M&T report before the bell today, with Citizens, Regions, Truist, and Fifth Third following Thursday and Friday -- and the single most important number to track across this cohort is not EPS but the sequential NII delta and deposit-cost trajectory read against JPMorgan's blow-out beat yesterday, because what the universals confirmed at mega-scale still has to be validated at the regional tier where deposit pricing pressure and funding mix are structurally more acute.**
---
### Top Takeaways
1. JPMorgan's Q2 2026 print was a blowout: EPS of six dollars and fourteen cents against a consensus of five dollars and eighty-five cents, and revenue of fifty-eight point zero two billion dollars versus fifty point one nine billion expected -- resetting the baseline upward significantly for the entire sector.
2. Morgan Stanley reports Q2 results today, July 15, providing the fee-income and wealth management read-across that completes the universal bank picture -- the data point super-regional CFOs need to benchmark their own fee revenue diversification strategies.
3. Fifth Third Bancorp recently acquired Comerica for ten point nine billion dollars, making its Q2 print this Friday the first fully material integration quarter -- the single most consequential M&A finance-function story in the super-regional cohort right now.
4. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signaled that inflation is now the primary policy concern, with risks "completely flipped," and the CME FedWatch tool currently assigns approximately twenty-five percent probability to a twenty-five basis point hike at the July twenty-eight to twenty-nine FOMC meeting.
5. Gartner predicts over forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027 -- a figure that has not yet registered in bank finance technology budgets but should be the governance conversation happening right now.
---
### Key Themes
**Theme 1 (New): The Super-Regional Earnings Gauntlet Begins**
Yesterday's universal bank prints set the bar. Today, the first super-regionals step up. PNC is reporting Q2 2026 results this morning before the market open, and in Q1 its earnings were driven by higher net interest income and fee income with rising loan and deposit balances -- but higher expenses acted as a headwind. The stable rate environment is likely to have supported PNC's NII growth, with management guiding NII to rise approximately three percent sequentially, and the Zacks consensus estimate for NII of four point one billion dollars indicates a sequential rise of nearly three point two percent. M&T Bank is also releasing Q2 results this morning, with analysts expecting earnings of four dollars and sixty-seven cents per share, up from four dollars and twenty-four cents in the year-ago period, against consensus revenue of two point four six billion dollars.
The read-across question: can super-regionals match the NIM resilience the universals just demonstrated, or does their structurally higher deposit repricing sensitivity compress margins relative to what JPMorgan just printed?
**Theme 2 (New): Fifth Third / Comerica -- The M&A Integration Finance Stress Test**
Fifth Third Bancorp recently acquired Comerica for ten point nine billion dollars. Seven regional banks report earnings this week, with Truist Financial and Fifth Third Bancorp drawing particular attention. Friday's Fifth Third print is the first real signal of how the combined finance function is performing under integration pressure: consolidated reporting, unified treasury operations, double-counted headcount, and duplicate system costs all flow through this quarter's numbers. For Deloitte clients, this is the textbook case for why finance transformation investment accelerates post-close, not before it.
Truist remains the worst performing of the seven regional bank stocks with a year-to-date gain of only five percent -- a signal that markets have not yet been convinced that its own prior integration costs are fully resolved, making its Friday print a credibility moment for the CFO narrative around efficiency.
**Theme 3 (Evolving): The G-SIB Capital Surcharge as a Finance Transformation Forcing Function**
JPMorgan's adjusted expense guidance for 2026 is approximately one hundred and five billion dollars, and management is planning for a G-SIB surcharge of five point two percent by 2028, up from four point five percent, implying roughly twenty billion dollars of incremental regulatory capital needs. This is not simply a capital story. A twenty-billion-dollar capital rebuild drives parallel demands on the finance function: regulatory reporting uplift, stress testing model recalibration, capital allocation repricing across business lines, and PPNR forecasting rework under an expanded capital buffer. The finance transformation demand here is real, not hypothetical. For super-regionals not subject to the same G-SIB surcharge, the competitive opportunity is the capital efficiency gap they can exploit against constrained universals.
---
### Banking Finance-Function Metrics
**NIM and NII:** With the Fed on hold and a stable rate curve, consensus expects NIM to hold around two point seven to two point nine percent. The two-to-ten-year curve is at positive thirty-eight basis points -- positively sloped but modest -- and further steepening would directly favor bank margins in Q3. The JPMorgan revenue beat of fifty-eight billion against a fifty-billion consensus suggests NII guidance was revised upward on the call; the key question now is whether that upward revision is exportable to the super-regional cohort.
**Deposit and Funding Economics:** For Bank of America, the risk sits precisely where the opportunity does -- rates. A one-hundred-basis-point rate decline would reduce BofA's NII by approximately two billion dollars over twelve months. That rate sensitivity profile is even more acute at super-regionals with shorter-duration loan books and more retail deposit reliance.
**Credit and Provisioning:** Commercial real estate portfolio maturity concentrations in 2026 to 2027, thirty-day delinquency rate evolution on credit cards, and H2 commercial loan growth guidance are the three credit quality questions that matter most for this earnings wave.
**Efficiency and Expenses:** Truist has been witnessing a continued rise in non-interest expenses because of investments in technology, inflationary pressure and expansion efforts, with management expecting GAAP non-interest expenses to rise three to four percent from three billion dollars. Rising technology investment as a percentage of non-interest expense is the common thread across the cohort -- and the efficiency ratio story for 2026 hinges on whether AI-driven workload reduction materializes fast enough to offset it.
**Capital:** The S&P Financial Sector ETF is up twelve point four percent year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500 at nine point six percent, and the price-to-tangible book ratio for the big four sits at one point seven times, slightly above the historical median of one point five times.
---
### Regulatory Radar
The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for July twenty-eight and twenty-nine, with the decision made on the second day, and there will be no Summary of Economic Projections produced for that meeting. That absence of a dot plot makes Chair Warsh's Congressional testimony this week the primary signal mechanism for the rate path. Warsh said policymakers remain "fully committed to restoring price stability" with "no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation," adding that "if we get policy right -- and we will -- the inflation surge of the last five years will be a thing of the past."
On April seventeenth, 2026, the Federal Reserve, OCC, and FDIC issued revised interagency model risk management guidance, designated SR 26-2 by the Federal Reserve and captured in OCC Bulletin 2026-13, superseding the long-standing SR 11-7. The revised guidance states that generative and agentic AI are novel and rapidly evolving and are not within its scope, and the agencies signaled plans to issue a request for information addressing banks' use of AI. This regulatory gap is itself a transformation driver: banks must govern agentic AI deployments without a defined rulebook, which pushes governance framework investment to the front of the finance technology agenda.
Banks are concentrating agentic AI on procedural, auditable work -- financial-crime detection, regulatory-change triage, controls testing, and continuous transaction monitoring -- and deployments emphasize governed environments where every agent decision is traceable, with a human approving outputs.
---
### AI in Finance
**Governed Deployment, Not Just Pilots:** In 2026, agentic AI in financial services moved into production, and the updates that matter most for compliance are no longer about what the technology might do but about how banks are governing what it already does. Major core providers shipped agent platforms, regulators drew a deliberate line around the technology, and real-time compliance monitoring shifted from a talking point to a deployed capability.
Fiserv launched agentOS, an operating system for agentic AI in banking, and FIS brought agentic AI to banking in partnership with Anthropic, starting with financial crimes, naming BMO and Amalgamated Bank among the first institutions to deploy its Financial Crimes AI Agent.
**The ROI Gap and the Sequencing Problem:** BCG's AI Radar 2026 found that spending on AI is set to double as a share of revenue, and ninety-four percent of organizations plan to continue investing despite uncertain short-term returns. At the same time, the gap between expectation and impact remains wide: while nearly ninety percent of CEOs expect AI agents to deliver measurable ROI, relatively few organizations can point to consistent results today.
The sequencing insight is the most actionable CFO signal in this cycle. As Bain Finance Transformation 2026 put it: "AI-first finance transformation requires deliberate sequencing. Data foundation first. Automation second. Intelligence third. CFOs who invest in AI before fixing data quality get poor results. Those who sequence correctly get compounding returns."
**Gartner's Cancellation Warning:** Gartner predicts over forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027. For bank CFOs, this is the number to put in front of vendor conversations. A Gartner survey of CFOs in early 2026 identified building AI talent within the finance function as their most pressing near-term challenge -- not technology or budget. As AI takes on more analytical and transactional work, the human role shifts from executing tasks to navigating outcomes: controllers who once compiled variance reports now need to validate AI-generated analyses, challenge underlying assumptions, and decide which findings warrant action.
**Where Finance Budgets Are Actually Moving:** A Salesforce study found CFOs dramatically shifted: whereas in 2020 over seventy percent pursued a conservative AI approach, by 2025 only four percent remained cautious. About thirty-three percent report an aggressive AI strategy now, and CFOs are dedicating approximately twenty-five percent of their budgets to AI agents, anticipating roughly twenty percent lifts in revenue or cost savings. The buying pattern shift is from broad GenAI licenses to purpose-built agentic agents in controls, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting -- exactly the domains where banks can demonstrate auditable ROI.
McKinsey early agentic AI use cases have shown significant potential, enabling zero-touch operations and reducing manual workloads by thirty to fifty percent, and in 2025 alone, fifty of the world's largest banks announced more than one hundred and sixty use cases.
---
### CFO Agenda, FP&A, and Transformation Signals
**The Expense-Efficiency Tension is the Q2 Story:** Across the earnings wave, the efficiency ratio is the transformation metric. NII is recovering. Fee income is growing. But non-interest expense growth driven by technology investment, integration costs, and inflationary compensation pressure is offsetting operating leverage at multiple institutions. The CFO conversation in H2 2026 is: at what point does the AI investment start showing up in the denominator of the efficiency ratio, not just the numerator of the technology cost line?
**FP&A Specifically -- the Intelligence Layer:** Within two to five years, AI agents will execute and optimize finance workflows in real time. BCG also flagged that "vibe coding" is coming to finance, and CFOs need guardrails to govern how finance teams use AI coding agents to build faster custom tools without compromising auditability, compliance, or core systems.
Deloitte's Finance Trends 2026 research shows most finance departments piloting AI use cases, with sixty-three percent actively using AI solutions. The distinction that matters for bank clients: active use versus scaled production with measurable impact on close cycle time or forecast accuracy. Only a fraction of that sixty-three percent has cleared that bar.
**M&A Integration as Transformation Catalyst:** Fifth Third / Comerica is the live proof point this week. Post-close integration of the finance function -- chart of accounts consolidation, treasury pooling, unified planning cycles, regulatory reporting harmonization -- is a two-to-three year journey that cannot be shortcut. Banks that have invested in a modern finance data foundation before the acquisition close materially reduce integration timelines. Those that have not face the most dangerous combination in transformation work: deadline pressure, data fragmentation, and regulatory scrutiny simultaneously.
---
### Contrarian Insight
The consensus narrative heading into super-regional earnings is that the JPMorgan blowout de-risks the sector. The contrarian case: the universals' beat was driven in meaningful part by trading revenue and capital markets fees -- neither of which translates to the super-regional business model. The overall impressive lending scenario in the quarter is likely to have supported NII for Truist, with commercial and industrial loans accounting for almost fifty percent of total loans and leases held for investment. But if deposit repricing has been more aggressive than universals across the regional cohort -- which the competitive dynamics of smaller-market deposit bases suggest -- the NIM delivery this week could disappoint even in an environment where the macro looks supportive. The real read will be deposit beta commentary, not headline NII.
---
### Client Conversation Hooks
1. **The G-SIB surcharge / capital rebuild story:** JPMorgan is planning for a G-SIB surcharge of five point two percent by 2028, up from four point five percent, implying twenty billion dollars of incremental capital. Ask your client: how is the capital adequacy rebuild changing the way the finance function allocates cost to business lines, and is their stress testing infrastructure built to reprice PPNR under a higher capital buffer?
2. **Fifth Third / Comerica as the M&A integration benchmark:** This is the first fully visible integration quarter for the largest super-regional deal of the cycle. Use Friday's print to anchor a conversation about what a post-close finance transformation roadmap looks like -- specifically, where data harmonization, planning system consolidation, and regulatory reporting integration create the biggest near-term risk.
3. **The forty percent AI project cancellation rate:** Gartner's prediction that over forty percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027 is the best single number to use when a bank client is accelerating AI spending without a sequencing framework. The follow-up question: is your client building on a clean data foundation, or deploying intelligence before automation is stable?
